Once upon a time there lived a family of mice. One day they wanted to go on a picnic. But as they were gathering the food, they noticed a big tube blocking their way. 

The family was worried but then one wise mouse had an idea. He asked the other mice to bring some warm items from their HOUSE such as strechy blankets and comfy beds.

The mice carefully piled up these items and used them to prevent the big tube from blocking their path. Then the family happily continued on their way to their picnic. 

The moral of this story is that you should use your creativity to prevent difficult situations and find smart solutions.

One day, she decided to go explore the world. She stumbled upon a hill filled with flowers. The flowers were all different colors and sizes.

Suddenly, the furry eraser started to glow. It was so beautiful! The colors were so bright and vibrant. The eraser started to dance and twirl around in the flowers. She was so happy. The glowing light filled everything around her.

When the sun set, the eraser stopped glowing. She was sad but at least she knew she could always glow again. She thanked the flowers for being so wonderful to her, and she gently went to sleep.

Sara and Tom like to play in the garden. They have a big box of toys and clothes. They like to dress up and pretend. One day, they find a pair of boots in the box. They are red and shiny. Sara and Tom want to try them on.

Sara picks the left boot and puts it on her foot. It is too big for her. She wobbles and falls down. Tom laughs and picks the right boot. He puts it on his foot. It is too big for him too. He wobbles and falls down. Sara and Tom laugh together.

They get up and walk around the garden. They feel like cowboys. They see a chili plant. It has red and green peppers. Sara and Tom like peppers. They pick some and eat them. They are spicy. Sara and Tom make funny faces. They spit out the peppers. They drink some water. They say "yuck" and "ouch".

They take off the boots and put them back in the box. They do not like spicy boots. They look for something else to play with. They find a hat and a scarf. They are soft and warm. Sara and Tom put them on. They feel like snowmen. They hug and smile. They like soft and warm things. They are happy.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They drive them on the floor, on the sofa, on the table. They make sounds like vroom, beep, honk.

One day, their mom gives them a big envelope. She says it is a surprise for them. She tells them to open it together. Tom and Sam are very excited. They wonder what is inside the envelope. They think maybe it is a new car, or a book, or a puzzle.

They run to their room and tear the envelope open. They see a picture of a real car. It is red and shiny. It has four doors and a big trunk. It looks very fast and cool. They also see a note from their dad. He writes that he loves them very much and that he has a big gift for them. He says he will come home soon and drive them in his new car.

Tom and Sam are very happy. They hug the picture and the note. They thank their mom and tell her they love her too. They can't wait to see their dad and his new car. They imagine how fun it will be to drive with him. They feel calm and safe. They put the picture and the note on their wall. They play with their toy cars until it is time for bed.

Jack was a 3 year old boy who loved playing. One day while he was playing on the playground, he saw some older kids doing funny movements. He liked it so he decided to copy them. He wasn't very good at it, but he kept trying.

The older kids laughed at him and Jack became very upset. He started to cry and ran away from the playground. He wanted to find his mommy to accept him no matter what.

Jack found his mommy, who gave him a big hug. His mommy told him that it was okay to accept motion no matter how hard it was. She said she was proud of him for trying.

Jack wiped away his tears and felt much better. He still wasn't very good at the motion the older kids were doing, but he was no longer upset. He was now happy and knew he was accepted no matter what.

One day, the kids decided to work together. So everyone got their friends and took turns poking the table.They forced their mightiest pokes against the mysterious table and something amazing happened.

The kids were so happy that they quickly started to play with the toys and eat the candy. They kept poking the table to see what else was inside. The kids had the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a pet fish named Goldie. Goldie lived in a bowl on Timmy's desk. One day, Timmy got bored and decided to take Goldie for a walk. He put Goldie in a rod and carried him outside. 

As they walked, Timmy saw a big, bright sun in the sky. He looked up and yawned because he was tired. Goldie also yawned and swam around in his rod. Timmy realized that Goldie was probably tired too, so he took him back inside and put him back in his bowl.

Matilda had a bed with a big, gray mattress. She loved bouncing on it and it felt so soft. Her mom always laughed when she saw Matilda jumping on it and said she was a crazy little girl.

One day, Matilda decided to go even crazier. She went and got a bucket of water and started to soak her mattress with it. She thought it would be even softer if it was wet.

Her mom suddenly saw Matilda and shouted, "What are you doing?!". Matilda smiled and said, "I'm making my mattress softer Mommy. I want to bounce even higher!" 

Her mom smiled. "Oh my Matilda, I'm afraid you won't be able to bounce if your mattress is wet. Come on now, let's dry it up!"

Matilda giggled. She and her mom worked together to dry the mattress and soon it was as good as new, only this time it was much softer. Matilda jumped and laughed, the gray mattress was just perfect for her.

Lila and Ben were playing on the porch with their dolls. They liked to pretend that the dolls were their babies and they had to take care of them. Lila had a delicate doll with a pink dress and long hair. Ben had a sturdy doll with a blue shirt and short hair.

"Look at my baby, she is so pretty and sweet," Lila said, holding her doll gently.

"My baby is strong and brave," Ben said, lifting his doll high.

Lila wanted to see Ben's doll, so she reached out to touch it. But Ben did not want to share. He pulled his doll away and pinched Lila's hand.

"Ow, that hurts!" Lila cried, dropping her doll. "Why did you pinch me?"

"Because you tried to take my baby," Ben said, hugging his doll.

"That's not nice, Ben. You should share with me. We are friends," Lila said, rubbing her hand.

"But I like my baby. He is mine," Ben said, frowning.

Lila felt sad and angry. She wanted to pinch Ben back, but she knew that would not make things better. She picked up her doll and looked at it. The doll's dress was torn and her hair was tangled.

"Look what you did, Ben. You ruined my baby. She is delicate, you know. You have to be careful with her," Lila said, tears in her eyes.

Ben looked at Lila's doll and felt sorry. He did not mean to hurt her or her doll. He liked Lila and he liked to play with her. He realized that he was selfish and mean.

"I'm sorry, Lila. I didn't mean to pinch you or ruin your baby. I was just scared that you would take my baby away. Can we be friends again?" Ben said, putting his doll down.

Lila smiled and nodded. She forgave Ben and hugged him. They decided to share their dolls and play together nicely. They learned that it was more fun to be kind and generous than to be greedy and rude.

Lily liked bananas very much. She ate one every day after lunch. But today, she saw a big bunch of bananas on the table. She wanted to eat more than one. She asked her mom, "Can I have two bananas, please?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily, one banana is enough for you. Too many bananas will make your tummy hurt. You can have another fruit if you want."

Lily was sad. She really wanted two bananas. She looked at the bunch of bananas. They looked so yellow and sweet. She had an idea. She waited until her mom was busy in the kitchen. Then she climbed on a chair and reached for the bananas.

But the bananas were too high for her. She stretched her arm as far as she could, but she could not grab them. She tried to pull the bunch of bananas down, but they were too heavy for her. She was not strong enough. She lost her balance and fell off the chair. She bumped her head on the floor. She started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her. She saw Lily on the floor and the chair tipped over. She saw the bananas on the table. She understood what happened. She hugged Lily and said, "Oh, Lily, are you okay? You should not try to take the bananas by yourself. You could have asked me for help. I would have allowed you to have one more banana if you really wanted it. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Bananas are good for you, but too many are not. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She was sorry for being naughty. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted two bananas. They looked so yummy. But I hurt my head and I could not get them. They were too high and too heavy. I'm not strong enough."

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are still a little girl. You will grow stronger and taller as you get older. But you have to eat healthy and follow the rules. Now, let me put some ice on your head. And then you can have one more banana if you still want it. But only one, okay?"

Lily smiled. She said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you. And I love bananas."

Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with their toys and draw pictures. One day, they found a big purple crayon in the park. They were very happy and decided to share it.

"Let's make a promise," Anna said. "We will always be friends and use this crayon together."

"OK, I promise," Ben said. "You are my best friend and this is our crayon."

They hugged and went home with their crayon. They drew many things with it: flowers, stars, animals, and rainbows. They had a lot of fun.

But the next day, Ben was miserable. He had a fever and a sore throat. He could not go to school or play with Anna. He missed her and the crayon very much.

Anna was miserable too. She wanted to see Ben and cheer him up. She thought of a way to make him happy. She took the purple crayon and drew a big heart on a piece of paper. She wrote "Get well soon, Ben. I miss you. Love, Anna." She asked her mom to take her to Ben's house.

She knocked on the door and Ben's mom opened it. She smiled and said, "Hello, Anna. Ben is in his room. He will be happy to see you."

Once upon a time, there was a funny cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with his friend, a little girl named Sue. Yesterday, they played with a big red ball in the yard.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw a big tree with many branches. She had a creative idea to build a tree house with her friends.

Lucy and her friends found wood and started to build the tree house. They used a rub to make the wood smooth. They worked together and had a lot of fun.

A little bird flew near and stared at Lucy and her friends. The bird liked their tree house too. When they finished, they all played in the tree house together. The bird stayed and became their new friend.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big box under a tree. They ran to the box and opened it. Inside, they found many toys and books and clothes. They were very happy and started to take what they wanted.

But they did not see a sign on the box that said: "These are donations for the poor children. Please do not touch." They were ignorant and did not know what donations or poor meant. They thought the box was a gift for them.

A lady came to the park and saw the boys with the box. She was angry and said: "What are you doing? These are not your things. You are stealing from the poor children. How can you be so selfish and greedy?"

The boys were scared and dropped the things. They tried to run away, but the lady caught them. She looked at their faces and saw that they were dirty and hungry. She felt sorry for them and said: "Are you poor too? Do you have a home and a family?"

The boys nodded and said: "Yes, we have a home and a family, but they are far away. We came here to search for a better life, but we have no money and no friends. We are sorry for taking the things. We did not know they were for the poor children. We thought they were for us."

The lady understood and said: "I see. You are not bad, just ignorant. You need to learn more about the world and how to help others. Come with me, I will take you to a place where you can get some food and clothes and education. Maybe you can also make some friends there."

The boys agreed and followed the lady. They learned that the box was part of a charity project that helped poor children in different countries. They felt ashamed and sorry for what they did. They also learned how to read and write and share and care. They made some friends who were also poor but kind. They realized that they were lucky to have a home and a family, and that they should be grateful and generous. They decided to give back some of the things they took and to help the charity project in any way they could. They became happier and smarter and better. They thanked the lady for teaching them and helping them. They never forgot the lesson they learned from the box.

Billy was walking through the park in early morning. He heard the sound of a whistle and looked around to see where the sound was coming from. He saw a little green bird hopping from branch to branch, whistling away. Billy smiled, it was the prettiest sound he had ever heard. 

Billy couldn't help but whistle back at the bird. He was surprised when the bird flew down to his shoulder and perched there. He wondered what it wanted, so he asked it. 

"Do you want milk?" he asked the bird. 

The bird gave a little nod and flew away. Billy went to the nearby convenience store and got a carton of milk. When he returned to the park, he saw the bird and all its friends nestled beside it. 

Billy opened the milk carton and the birds were so excited! They all started chirping, hopping from branch to branch with happiness. The little green bird came up to Billy and kissed him on his cheek. It was the most amazing thing he had ever seen.

Finally, she remembered that the rain was getting heavy and she needed to go back inside. When she was about to enter the house, her mom said, "See, even when it rains, it can be beautiful. If you look deep enough, you'll find magic and beauty inside any situation."

The little girl smiled and nodded, understanding the lesson her mom had taught her. No matter how hard the rain shines and storms, there will always be some form of beauty to be found.

Lily liked to organize her toys. She had a box for her dolls, a box for her cars, and a box for her books. She liked to make everything neat and tidy. She did not like it when her brother Max messed up her toys. He liked to throw them around and mix them up.

One day, Lily and Max had steak for dinner. Lily loved steak. She ate it all up and said thank you to Mom. Max did not like steak. He said it was terrible and made a face. He did not eat it and said he wanted candy instead. Mom said no, he had to eat his steak first. Max got angry and threw his steak on the floor. Lily was shocked. She thought that was very rude and wasteful.

Mom was upset too. She said Max had to go to his room and think about what he did. She said he could not have any candy or dessert until he apologized and cleaned up his mess. Max stomped to his room and slammed the door. He did not say sorry or pick up his steak.

Lily felt sorry for Mom. She wanted to help her. She asked Mom if she could organize the kitchen. Mom smiled and said yes, that would be very nice of her. Lily got a cloth and a bucket and started to wipe the table and the chairs. She put the dishes in the sink and the leftovers in the fridge. She even found Max's steak on the floor and threw it in the trash. She did a good job and made the kitchen look clean and cozy.

Mom hugged Lily and thanked her for being such a good helper. She said she was very proud of her. She said she could have a piece of cake and some milk for dessert. Lily was happy. She enjoyed her cake and milk and felt warm and cozy. She learned that it was better to be organized and polite than to be messy and rude. She hoped that Max would learn that too.

Charlie was in school, feeling very miserable. Everyone was writing on the blackboard, but all Charlie wanted to do was shrug. He tried to tell the teacher, but she just shook her head and moved on. Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They saw many things there: trees, flowers, birds, dogs, and people. One day, they saw something new: a big statue of a lion. It was fierce and had a long mane and sharp teeth.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom said. "It looks like it can roar and bite!"

Mia was not afraid. She said, "It is just a statue. It cannot move or talk. It is not real."

Tom wanted to have some fun. He said, "Let's play a game. You be the lion and I be the hunter. You have to stay still like the statue and I have to sneak up on you. If I touch you, you have to dance and make noise. If you move before I touch you, you lose."

Mia agreed. She went to the statue and stood next to it. She tried to look fierce like the lion. Tom hid behind a bench and waited for his chance.

He saw Mia's eyes blink. He thought she was bored. He decided to surprise her. He ran towards her and shouted, "I got you, lion!"

But Mia was not bored. She was smart. She saw Tom coming and had a plan. She waited until he was very close and then she jumped and roared. She scared Tom so much that he fell on the ground.

Mia laughed and said, "You lose, hunter! I am the fierce lion and you are the scared mouse!"

Tom was not happy. He said, "That is not fair! You cheated! You moved before I touched you!"

Mia said, "No, I did not. I moved after you shouted. You gave yourself away. You have to dance and make noise now. That is the rule."

Tom did not want to dance and make noise. He was still scared and angry. He said, "No, I don't. This game is silly. I don't want to play anymore."

He got up and walked away. Mia followed him and said, "Come on, Tom. Don't be a sore loser. It was just a game. Let's play something else."

But Tom did not listen. He did not want to play with Mia anymore. He wanted to go home.

Mia was sad. She liked Tom and wanted to be his friend. She wished he would not be so mad. She looked at the statue and had an idea. She said, "Hey, Tom. Look at the statue. It is smiling. It likes our game. It wants us to play again."

Tom looked at the statue. He saw that it was smiling. He thought it was funny. He smiled too. He said, "You are right, Mia. It is smiling. Maybe it is not so fierce after all. Maybe it likes to dance and make noise too."

Mia said, "Yes, it does. Let's dance and make noise with it. Maybe it will join us."

Tom said, "OK, let's try. Maybe it will be fun."

They went to the statue and started to dance and make noise. They pretended to be lions and hunters and friends. They had a lot of fun. The statue did not move or talk, but it seemed to enjoy their game. It watched them with a smile.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to play in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers, the birds and the bugs. One day, they saw a big red poppy that was very pretty. Lily wanted to pick it and take it home, but Ben said no.

"No, Lily, we can't pick the poppy. It is not ours. It belongs to the garden. If we pick it, it will die and the bees will have no food. We can look at it, but we can't touch it."

Lily was angry. She did not listen to Ben. She said, "I don't care. I want the poppy. It is so pretty. I will pick it and put it in a vase. It will make our room look nice."

She reached out her hand to grab the poppy, but Ben stopped her. He held her hand and said, "Please, Lily, don't do it. It is not nice to take what is not yours. It is not fair to the garden and the bees. The poppy is happy here. Let it be."

Lily refused to listen. She pulled her hand away and said, "You are mean, Ben. You don't want me to have anything. I will pick the poppy and you can't stop me."

She tried to pick the poppy again, but this time, something happened. A bee came out of the poppy and stung Lily on her finger. Lily cried out in pain and dropped the poppy. She ran to Ben and said, "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts! The bee stung me! Help me, Ben!"

Ben felt sorry for Lily. He hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I will help you. Come, let's go to Mom. She will make it better. But next time, listen to me. Don't pick the flowers. They are not for us. They are for the garden and the bees. They are not toys. They are alive."

Lily nodded. She was sorry for what she did. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. You were right. I was wrong. I won't pick the flowers again. I will look at them and enjoy them, but I won't touch them."

Ben smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Come on, let's go. Mom has made some yummy cookies for us. We can share them and be happy."

They held hands and walked to the house. They ate the yummy cookies and thanked Mom. They learned to respect the garden and the bees. They learned to listen to each other and be kind. They were happy twins.

Lily liked to ride her bike. She had a pink bike with a basket and a bell. She was very independent. She did not need help from anyone. She could pedal fast and balance well.

One day, she wanted to go to the park with her bike. She asked her mom if she could go. Her mom said yes, but she had to stay on the sidewalk and be careful. Lily said okay and put on her helmet. She was excited to see the swings and the slide.

She rode her bike along the sidewalk. She saw a big dog on the way. The dog was barking and running towards her. Lily was scared. She tried to pedal faster, but the dog was faster. The dog jumped on her bike and knocked her down. Lily fell on the grass and hurt her knee. She started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her. She picked her up and hugged her. She checked her knee and saw a small cut. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's just a scratch. You're brave and strong. The dog was just playing. He didn't mean to hurt you."

Lily looked at her mom and frowned. She said, "But mom, I don't like dogs. They're scary and mean. I don't want to play with them. I want to play with my bike."

Her mom smiled and said, "I know, Lily. But not all dogs are scary and mean. Some dogs are friendly and nice. Maybe you can make friends with the dog next time. He might like your bike too. He might want to share it with you."

Lily thought about it and said, "Maybe. But I like my bike more. It's mine. I don't want to share it."

Her mom said, "That's okay, Lily. You can keep your bike. But sometimes, it's good to share with others. It makes them happy and it makes you happy too. Sharing is caring, Lily. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. But can we go to the park now? I want to see the swings and the slide."

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. Let's go to the park. But first, let me clean your knee and put a band-aid on it. Then, you can ride your bike again. And don't forget to ring your bell. It makes a nice sound."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You're my independent girl."

Anna smiled and said, "Okay, dad. Thank you, Mr. Lee. I want to see your boat and your fish. Let's go."

Lily liked to play with her mom's makeup. She liked to put it on her face and pretend she was a princess. She liked the red lipstick, the pink blush, and the shiny eyeshadow. She thought they made her look pretty.

One day, Lily saw a sign that said "garage sale". She asked her mom what it meant. Her mom said it meant they were selling things they did not want anymore. Lily thought that was a good idea. She decided to sell some of her mom's makeup. She thought other people would like it too.

She took a box and put some makeup in it. She wrote "makeup for sale" on a paper and taped it to the box. She carried the box to the sidewalk and waited for customers. She hoped to make some money.

The lady said, "You don't need makeup to be a princess. You are already a princess. You are beautiful and smart and kind. You just need to be yourself."

She gave Lily a hug and a kiss. She said, "Now, let's go and talk to your mom. I'm sure she will forgive you. And maybe she will let you play with some of her makeup sometimes. But only with her permission and supervision. OK?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "OK. Thank you, lady. You are very nice."

They took the box and walked back to Lily's house. Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned to respect her mom's things and to be careful with makeup. She also learned that she was a princess without makeup. And she made a new friend.

Anna liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long hair, a pink dress and a smile. Anna took Lily everywhere with her.

One day, Anna and Lily went to the park with Mommy. They saw a big slide, a swing and a sandbox. Anna wanted to try the slide. She put Lily on her lap and slid down. But the slide was too fast and Anna and Lily fell off at the end. Lily hit a rock and her dress tore. Anna saw a big cut on Lily's arm. She cried and hugged Lily.

"Mommy, Mommy, Lily is hurt!" Anna shouted.

Mommy came running and saw Lily's arm. She said, "Oh, poor Lily. Don't worry, Anna, we can heal her. Let's go home and get some bandages and glue."

Anna nodded and followed Mommy. She held Lily close to her chest.

At home, Mommy took out a pot from the kitchen. She filled it with water and put it on the stove. She said, "We need to boil some water to clean Lily's arm. It will kill the germs and make it better."

Anna watched as the water bubbled and steamed. She thought it was unusual. She had never seen water do that before. She asked, "Mommy, why does the water do that?"

Mommy said, "That's what happens when water gets very hot. It turns into steam. Steam is like a cloud, but hotter. We have to be careful not to touch it, because it can burn us."

Anna said, "Oh, I see. Can I help you heal Lily?"

Mommy said, "Of course, you can. You are a good helper. Here, take this cloth and dip it in the water. Then, gently wipe Lily's arm with it. That will clean the cut."

Anna did as Mommy said. She was careful not to touch the steam or the pot. She wiped Lily's arm with the cloth. She saw the dirt and blood come off. She said, "Look, Mommy, Lily's arm is cleaner now."

Mommy said, "Good job, Anna. Now, we need to put some glue on the cut. That will stick the skin together and stop the bleeding. Then, we need to wrap a bandage around it. That will protect the cut and make it heal faster."

Mommy took out a tube of glue and a roll of bandage. She squeezed some glue on Lily's arm and pressed the edges of the cut together. She said, "This glue is special. It is safe for dolls and people. It will dry quickly and make a thin layer of skin. It will not hurt Lily."

Anna said, "Wow, that's amazing. Lily is lucky to have you, Mommy."

Mommy said, "Thank you, Anna. You are very sweet. Now, let's put the bandage on. Can you hold Lily's arm still for me?"

Anna held Lily's arm still while Mommy wrapped the bandage around it. She made sure it was not too tight or too loose. She said, "There, we are done. Lily is all healed. How do you feel, Lily?"

Anna made Lily say, "I feel much better, Mommy. Thank you for healing me. And thank you, Anna, for being my friend. I love you both."

Mommy said, "You are very welcome, Lily. We love you too. Now, why don't you and Anna go play in your room? I'll make some cookies for you."

Anna said, "Yay, cookies! Come on, Lily, let's go play. We can have a tea party with your new bandage. You look very pretty."

Anna and Lily went to Anna's room and played happily. They forgot about the slide and the rock. They were glad they had each other and Mommy. They knew Mommy could heal anything.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. One day, they saw a big, hairy dog. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Ben and Lily wanted to pet the dog, but they were a little scared.

"Can we touch the dog?" Ben asked Lily.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask the owner first," Lily said.

They looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He was reading a book and did not notice the dog or the children.

"Excuse me, sir. Is this your dog?" Lily called out.

The man looked up and smiled. "Yes, this is Max. He is very nice and loves to play. Do you want to pet him?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said.

They ran to the dog and started to stroke his fur. Max licked their faces and wagged his tail harder. Ben and Lily laughed and hugged the dog.

"Thank you for letting us pet your dog. He is very soft and warm," Lily said.

"You're welcome. I'm glad you like him. He is a good dog, but he needs a lot of care. He needs to eat, drink, walk, and brush every day. Do you know how to care for a dog?" the man asked.

Ben and Lily nodded. They had learned about animals at school. They knew that dogs were like people. They needed love and attention.

"We know how to care for a dog. We would give him food and water, take him for walks, and brush his fur. We would also play with him and cuddle him. We would be good friends," Ben said.

"That's wonderful. You sound like very kind and responsible children. Do you have a dog of your own?" the man asked.

Ben and Lily shook their heads. They did not have a dog. They lived in a small apartment with their parents. They did not have enough space or money for a dog.

"We wish we had a dog. We love dogs. But we can't have one. Maybe when we grow up," Lily said.

The man looked at them with a twinkle in his eye. He had an idea. He closed his book and stood up.

"Well, I have a surprise for you. I am moving to another city next week. I can't take Max with me. He is too big and hairy for the plane. I have been looking for a new home for him. Do you think your parents would let you have him?" he asked.

Ben and Lily gasped. They could not believe their ears. They looked at each other and then at the dog. They wanted to say yes, but they were not sure.

"We don't know. We have to ask them first. They might say no. We don't have a lot of room or money," Ben said.

The man nodded. He understood. He did not want to pressure them. He wanted them to be happy.

"I see. Well, why don't you go home and talk to them? Here is my phone number. You can call me tomorrow and let me know what they say. If they say yes, you can have Max. He is yours. If they say no, I will find another home for him. But I hope they say yes. You are the best friends he could have," he said.

He handed them a piece of paper with his number. He also gave them a leash and a collar for Max. He hugged them and kissed the dog.

"Goodbye, Max. I love you. Be good to your new friends. They will take good care of you," he said.

He walked away, waving and smiling. Ben and Lily waved back, holding the leash and the collar. They looked at Max. He looked at them. They felt a warm feeling in their hearts. They hoped their parents would say yes. They wanted to care for Max. They wanted to be his family. They ran home, excited and nervous. They had a big question to ask. They had a big, hairy dog to love.

Tom and Mia liked to play with blocks. They liked to make towers and houses and bridges. Sometimes they made a game of who could make the highest tower. They used all the blocks they had.

One day, they saw a new box of blocks in the corner. It was big and shiny and had a picture of a giant on it. Tom and Mia wanted to see what was inside. They opened the box and found many big and colorful blocks. They were very happy.

"Let's use these blocks to make our towers," Tom said.

"Yes, let's," Mia agreed.

They took the blocks and started to add them to their towers. They made them taller and taller and taller. They did not notice that the box had a label that said: "Do not open. These blocks belong to Ben."

Ben was their big brother. He was six years old and he liked to build things too. He had saved his money to buy the box of blocks. He had hidden it in the corner until he could find a good place to play with it. He was at school when Tom and Mia opened his box.

When he came home, he saw his box was open and his blocks were gone. He looked around and saw Tom and Mia's towers. They had used his blocks. He was very angry.

"Hey, those are my blocks!" he shouted. "You took them without asking. That's not fair."

Tom and Mia heard Ben's voice and felt guilty. They knew they had done something wrong. They looked at their towers and then at Ben. They did not know what to say.

"We're sorry, Ben," Mia said. "We didn't know they were yours. We just wanted to play."

"Yeah, we're sorry," Tom said. "We thought they were for everyone. We didn't mean to make you mad."

Ben looked at them and saw they were sorry. He was still angry, but he also loved his brother and sister. He decided to be nice.

"It's okay, I guess," he said. "But next time, you have to ask before you use something that's not yours. And you have to share."

"Okay, we will," Tom and Mia said.

"Can we play with your blocks, please?" Mia asked.

"Sure, you can," Ben said. "But only if I can play with you."

"Okay, you can," Tom and Mia said.

They smiled and hugged Ben. Then they all played with the blocks together. They made a giant tower that reached the ceiling. They had fun.

"Hi, Lily!" he signed. "What do you have?"

"Spaghetti!" Lily signed back. "Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Sam signed. He took the box and invited Lily inside. They went to the kitchen and warmed up the spaghetti in the microwave. Then they sat at the table and ate.

"This is yummy!" Sam signed. "Thank you, Lily!"

"You're welcome, Sam!" Lily signed. "I'm glad you like it!"

They finished their spaghetti and drank some juice. Then they played with Sam's toys. They had a lot of fun. Lily liked Sam. He was her best friend.

But then Lily started to feel sick. Her tummy hurt and she felt weak. She did not know why. She told Sam she had to go home. Sam looked worried.

"Are you okay, Lily?" he signed. "Do you need help?"

Lily shook her head. She said she just needed to rest. She thanked Sam for playing and said goodbye. She walked slowly to her house. She felt worse and worse.

When she got home, she saw her mom. Her mom looked angry.

"Lily, where have you been?" her mom asked. "And what is that on your shirt?"

Lily looked down. She saw red sauce on her shirt. It was from the spaghetti.

"I went to Sam's house," Lily said. "We ate spaghetti."

"Spaghetti?" her mom said. "Lily, you know you are allergic to tomatoes! That's why you feel sick!"

Lily felt scared. She did not know she was allergic to tomatoes. She did not know what that meant.

"I'm sorry, mom," Lily said. "I didn't know."

Her mom hugged her. She said it was not her fault. She said she would take her to the doctor. She said the doctor would make her feel better.

Lily nodded. She hoped the doctor would make her feel better. She also hoped Sam would not be mad at her. She still loved spaghetti. But she loved Sam more.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They had a network of roads and bridges made of blocks and cardboard. They liked to make their cars zoom and honk on the network.

The ball hit the network and knocked down some blocks and bridges. The network was ruined. Lily was sad. She cried. She said, "Ben, you are mean! You broke my network!"

Ben felt sorry. He saw that he made Lily cry. He did not want to make her cry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have thrown the ball. Can we fix the network?"

Lily stopped crying. She looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She said, "OK, Ben. We can fix the network. But next time, ask me nicely if you want to play something else."

Lily smiled. She said, "Maybe we can. But first, let's fix the network."

They hugged and started to fix the network. They were friends again.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They liked to make noises and race them on the floor. One day, they found a big car that had a battery inside. It could move by itself when they pushed a button.

"Wow, this car is mighty!" Ben said. "It is faster and louder than the others. Let's play with it outside!"

"Okay!" Lily said. They took the car and ran to the backyard. They found a spot of dirt and put the car on it. They pushed the button and watched the car zoom around.

"Vroom, vroom!" they shouted. They had fun chasing the car and making it turn and spin. They played until the sun was low in the sky.

"Ben, Lily, time to come in!" their mom called. "It's getting dark and dinner is ready!"

"Okay, mom!" they said. They ran to the car and picked it up. But the car did not move or make noise anymore. The battery was dead.

"Oh no, the car is broken!" Ben said. "What can we do?"

"I have an idea!" Lily said. "Let's bury the car in the dirt. Maybe it will grow a new battery!"

"Really?" Ben said. "Will that work?"

"Sure!" Lily said. "Everything grows in the dirt. Flowers, trees, carrots. Why not batteries?"

"Okay, let's try it!" Ben said. They dug a hole in the dirt and put the car in it. They covered it with more dirt and patted it down.

"There, the car is buried!" Lily said. "Now we have to wait and see what happens!"

They ran inside and ate their dinner. They forgot about the car and played with their other toys. The next day, they remembered the car and ran outside to dig it up. They hoped to see a new battery or maybe even a bigger car.

But when they reached the spot of dirt, they saw nothing. The car was gone. Someone had taken it.

"Hey, where is our car?" Ben said. "Who took it?"

"I don't know!" Lily said. "Maybe a dog or a bird or a monster!"

They looked around and saw no sign of their car. They felt sad and angry. They had lost their mighty car. They wished they had not buried it. They wished they had taken it inside and asked their mom for a new battery.

They learned a hard lesson. Burying things in the dirt does not make them grow. It only makes them disappear.

One day, Lily and Ben saw snow falling from the sky. They had never seen snow before, and they were very curious. They ran to the window and watched the white flakes cover the ground and the trees. They wanted to touch the snow, to make snowballs and snowmen, to slide and skate on the ice.

"Can we go outside, please?" they asked their parents.

"But we want to play in the snow!" Lily and Ben said. "It looks so fun and pretty!"

"No, you don't," their parents said. "Snow is boring and ugly, and you will hurt yourself. You have to stay inside and learn your numbers."

"Lily! Ben! Where are you?" they shouted. "How dare you go outside without our permission? Come back here right now!"

Lily and Ben were scared and sorry. They knew they had done something bad, and they would be in trouble. They did not want to go back, but they had no choice. They left their snowballs and snowmen, and they ran to the door.

They opened the door and saw their parents' faces. They were red and stern, and they were holding their books and numbers.

"We are very disappointed in you," they said. "You have disobeyed us and wasted your time. You have to go to your rooms and study. No more snow, no more play."

Lily and Ben nodded and hung their heads. They followed their parents to their rooms and closed the doors. They looked at their books and numbers, but they did not want to read or learn. They wanted to play in the snow.

They looked out of the window and saw their snowballs and snowmen. They were still there, but they were melting and shrinking. They felt a tear roll down their cheek.

She walked slowly to the lumber and stepped on it. She felt wobbly and nervous. She did not like it at all.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice.

"Tom! Mia! What are you doing on the lumber? Get down from there right now!"

It was Dad. He had come home from work. He looked very grumpy. He had seen them from the window.

Tom and Mia felt sorry and scared. They jumped off the lumber and ran to Dad. They hugged him and said they were sorry.

Dad was not happy. He told them they had been naughty and careless. He said they could have hurt themselves or damaged the lumber. He said they had to go inside and have a time out.

One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They brought their wheel with them and ran to the grass. They saw another boy playing with a ball. He was alone and looked lonely. Tom and Lily wanted to be his friend.

John didn't like staying in the church at all. He just wanted to go back home. Then, his parents took him outside and he felt much better. When he looked back at the church, he shivered one last time. He was sure glad that he didn't have to stay there!

Once upon a time there was a poor little kitten named Mittens who was stuck on the side of a tall building. She mewed sadly and didn't know what to do.

Just then, a nice man named Jacob saw the scared kitten. He ran over to help her. He said: "Mittens, don't worry. I'll rescue you!"

Jacob carefully grabbed the kitten and carried her away from the edge of the tall building. Mittens was so happy and meowed with joy.

Jacob looked around for something for Mittens to eat. He saw a bakery and ran inside. He grabbed a fruit pastry and handed it to Mittens. She licked it up hungrily and thanked Jacob.

Mittens couldn't stop purring and was happy to be safe and have a yummy snack. Jacob knew he had found a friend and they both went on an adventure together.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah liked to measure things - big things, small things and everything in between! 

One day, Sarah decided to measure the path around her house. She grabbed her ruler from her desk and went out. As she slowly walked along the path, she started to measure it.

Suddenly, Sarah heard a noise. It was her dad! He was standing right behind her, watching her measure. "I'm so proud of you Sarah," he said. 

Sarah looked up and smiled. Her dad was so impatient to see how long the path was! She finished measuring the path, and announced the number to her dad - it was seven feet long! 

Her dad clapped and said, "good job, Sarah! Now you know how to measure things, you can make all kinds of measurements."

Sarah continued to measure things around her house, gaining more knowledge with each measurement. She had so much fun exploring the world with her ruler.

Lily liked to admire the yellow flowers in the garden. She thought they were very pretty and bright. She liked to smell them and touch them gently. Sometimes she picked one and gave it to her mom or dad.

One day, she saw a big yellow flower that was different from the others. It had a wide face with many petals and a brown center. It looked like a sun. Lily wanted to see it closer, so she walked to it and bent down.

But as she got near, she heard a loud buzz. She saw a black and yellow bug flying around the flower. It had a pointy tail and wings. Lily was scared of the bug. She thought it might sting her. She ran away from the flower and back to her mom.

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. That was a bee. Bees are not bad. They help the flowers grow and make honey. They only sting if you bother them. You can admire the flower from a distance, but don't touch it."

Lily nodded and felt better. She looked at the flower again and smiled. She still liked it, but she was careful not to get too close. She admired it from afar and said, "It's a beautiful flower, mom. But I like the other yellow flowers more. They are nicer and quieter."

Once upon a time, there was a friendly shape. His name was Spring and he loved to play outside in the sunshine. Every day he would jump and hop around in the grass and have fun.

One day, Spring wanted some friends to play with. He saw two small shapes and he thought they would be friendly. He ran over to them and eagerly asked if they wanted to play.

The two shapes smiled at Spring and said yes. They played tag and catch until the sun went down. Spring was so happy to have found new friends.

Every day, the three friends would meet up in the same spot and play until nightfall. Spring was the happiest shape in the world because he had found two wonderful new friends.

The end.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have a big box of toys in the yard. One day, they find a new toy in the box. It is a red fire truck with a ladder and a hose.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom says. "It is a fire truck. We can be firefighters and save people."

"Yes, let's play!" Jen says. "But we need fuel for the fire truck. Where can we get fuel?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He sees a bottle of water on the table. He has an idea. He runs to the table and grabs the bottle. He pours some water into the fire truck's tank.

"Here, I have fuel!" he says. "Now we can drive the fire truck and put out fires."

Jen smiles. She gets in the fire truck with Tom. They turn on the siren and the lights. They drive around the yard, looking for fires. They see a pile of leaves. They pretend it is a fire.

"Oh no, there is a fire!" Tom says. "We have to put it out. Jen, you use the hose. I will use the ladder."

"OK, Tom!" Jen says. She rubs the hose and sprays water on the leaves. Tom climbs the ladder and pretends to rescue a cat.

"Meow, meow!" he says. He holds the cat and comes down the ladder. He gives the cat to Jen.

"Good job, Jen!" he says. "We put out the fire and saved the cat. We are brave firefighters."

"Good job, Tom!" Jen says. She hugs the cat and rubs its fur. The cat purrs and licks her face. It is a calm and happy cat.

They put the cat in the fire truck and drive back to the box. They park the fire truck and put the bottle back on the table. They are tired but proud. They sit on the grass and play with the cat.

"We had fun today," Tom says.

"Yes, we did," Jen says. "We are good friends."

They smile and hug each other. They love to play with cars and trucks. They love their new toy. It is a red fire truck with a ladder and a hose.

She looked up and saw a hummingbird hovering above her. The hummingbird continued, "You were racing around that old, filthy nest. That doesn't seem very safe. Why don't we race around this tree branch instead?"

The little chick was so excited! She figured the branch would make a much better racetrack. The chick and the hummingbird raced around the branch together. They had a wonderful time, and from then on, they raced together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the sunshine and pick flowers. One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest and saw a sad bunny. The bunny was crying because it was lost and didn't know how to get home. 

Lily felt sorry for the bunny and wanted to help. She picked up the bunny and held it close to her chest. She whispered kind words to the bunny and tried to comfort it. 

Lily knew the way back to her house, so she carried the bunny all the way home. When they arrived, Lily gave the bunny some carrots to eat and made a cozy bed for it to sleep in. 

The bunny was so grateful to Lily for her honest kindness. From that day on, the bunny and Lily became best friends and they would often play together in the pine forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. Anna was three years old, and she loved to draw. Every day after lunch she would grab the chalk and march around the garden. As she marched, Anna created beautiful pictures.

One day, Anna had a really big idea: she wanted to march around the whole house! Her mum thought this was a great idea, she just had to remind Anna to stay safe. Anna grabbed the chalk and started off on her adventure.  

As she marched, Anna noticed that as she moved her chalk drawings were getting weaker and weaker. Anna kept going, but she was looking for something. After what seemed like forever, she turned a corner and spotted a bright yellow bucket of water. She quickly filled up her chalk and it became strong again. Anna was so happy she could keep marching around the house. 

What a funny little adventure! Anna loved her journey and she learned something important. Whenever the chalk seemed weak, she just needed to fill up the bucket and the chalk would be strong again.

Once upon a time, there was a dead park. No one went there anymore. The grass was brown and the flowers had dried up.

One day, a little boy and his dad saw the dead park and the dad said it was time to help. 

They started to pick up all the waste that was laying around. Little by little, it got tidier. 

Finally, when all the waste was gone, the dad went to the town hall to ask for permission. The people at the town hall said yes. 

The dad and the little boy went back to the dead park and started to plant flowers, new grass and trees. After a few weeks, the dead park was alive again. 

The dad and the little boy were so proud of their hard work. They could now see birds flying around and butterflies drinking the nectar of the flowers.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy called Joe. Joe loved playing in the sand on the beach. He would turn it over and over with his hands, making sandcastles and sculptures that he thought were the best.

One day, Joe heard a voice coming from the sand. "Help me, please," it said. Joe stopped what he was doing and looked around. He saw no one, only sand. He took a step closer and said," Who's there?"

"I'm stuck in the sand and can't get out by myself. Please turn the sand and help me out," the voice said again.

So Joe turned the sand and soon he saw a little crab. He picked it up and showed it to the people on the beach. Everyone was so surprised. Joe had been so kind and strong to help the crab.

From then on, Joe was known as the strong helper who didn't give up until the crab had been freed from the sand.

Once upon a time there was a great gem. The gem was so sparkly and bright! Everyone wanted to see it. 

One day a little girl named Hannah saw the gem. She smiled and reached out to touch it. But the gem was too high for her to reach.  

Hannah cried and cried, but the gem didn't come down. Suddenly a magical fairy came out of nowhere and said "I can help you!" 

The fairy waved her wand and the great gem floated down to where Hannah could touch it. She was so happy, she couldn't stop smiling. 

The fairy said, "Take the gem and remember, when you need help, I can always be there". 

Hannah thanked the fairy and with the gem in her hand, she ran off to show her friends.

John was a young boy who loved to tell jokes. Every day he would go out, looking for new jokes to tell his friends. He loved the laughter it brought him and his friends.

One day, John decided to go farther than he ever had before. He set off, feeling excited and a little bit dizzy at the same time.

The farther he went, the more wild and strange things he found. He thought he saw a giant growing in the distance. But he laughed it off, thinking it was just a tall tree.

But as he kept walking, the giant started to get bigger and bigger. John realized too late that it wasnâ€™t a joke. He had stumbled into danger.

The giant was getting closer, it was headed his way. John tried to run away but he was too weak and dizzy. The giant caught up and John was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Benny. Benny loved to eat corn all day long. One day, Benny saw his friend, a little bird named Lily, skipping happily in the field.

Benny asked, "Lily, why are you so happy?"

Lily replied, "I found a big bag of corn! Do you want to share it with me?"

Benny was excited and said, "Yes, please!" But when they got to the bag of corn, they saw that it was too high for them to reach.

Benny said, "Oh no, how will we get the corn?"

Lily had an idea and said, "Let's skip together and try to reach it!"

So, they held hands and skipped as high as they could. Finally, they were able to grab the bag of corn and share it happily. Benny learned that sometimes it's good to have a friend to help you when you have a problem.

Once upon a time, there lived an old man called Jack. He sold delicious spicy food from his cart to the people of the village.

One day, a young man carrying a backpack knocked on Jack's door. 

"Do you sell youth?" asked the young man.

Jack shook his head. "No, I'm afraid not," he said.

The young man thanked Jack, and continued his journey.

Days passed, and Jack noticed the same young man had returned to the village. He carried the same backpack, but it felt lighter this time.

Curious, Jack asked the young man what he had in his magical backpack. 

"Youth," the young man replied, with a big smile.

Jack was surprised, but he thought about his own age and he knew he would need youth soon. So, he asked the man if he could buy some. 

The young man agreed and said, "Yes, I sell the most spicy youth you will ever taste!"

Jack was excited and from that day on, he bought all the spicy youth from the young man, so that he could stay young forever.

Harry was a curious three-year-old boy. He was looking around the house for something to do. His parents said he wanted to explore. So he did. 

Harry walked into the kitchen and stopped in front of the refrigerator. It was big, really huge. He wanted to try and open it. But it was too high for him to reach.

"Mom, can you help me open the enormous refrigerator?" he asked. 

His mom walked over. She said, "No problem. Let me help you."

She tried opening the door, but it wouldn't open. She turned the knob harder, but it still wouldn't open. Then she said, "It looks like the door is stuck. Let's keep trying."

So they tried together, and it opened! Harry was so happy. He saw shelves full of all his favorite food. He reached out and grabbed a container of juice.

"Thanks, Mom!" he said, happily.

Harry had discovered a great challenge. All he needed was a little help from his mom, and together they had found success.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside near the river. One day, she saw her friend, a duck, swimming in the river.

"Hello, duck! What are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I am swimming in the river. It's so much fun!" replied the duck.

Lily wanted to join the duck, but she was hungry. "I want to swim, but I'm hungry. I need to eat something delicious first," she said.

"I know where we can find something delicious. Follow me!" said the duck.

They walked along the river until they found a berry bush. They picked the berries and ate them. "These berries are delicious!" said Lily. "Now I am complete and ready to swim with you, duck!" And they swam together in the river until it was time to go home.

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to go outside and play. They liked to run, jump, climb and explore. One day, their mom said they could go to the big park with the mountain. Anna and Ben were very enthusiastic. They put on their hats, shoes and backpacks and got in the car.

At the park, they saw the mountain. It was very tall and green. They wanted to climb to the top and see what was there. They asked their mom if they could go. She said yes, but they had to stay together and be careful. Anna and Ben nodded and started to walk up the hill.

As they climbed, they saw many things. They saw flowers, birds, rocks and bugs. They also saw other people who were climbing or biking or having picnics. They said hello to them and kept going. They felt happy and curious.

They reached the top of the mountain and looked around. They saw the park, the city, the sky and the clouds. They also saw something else. It was a big, round, shiny thing. It looked like a ball, but it was not a ball. It was a balloon. It was red and blue and yellow and had a string. It was floating in the air.

"Wow, look at that!" Anna said.

"Where did it come from?" Ben asked.

"Maybe someone let it go by mistake," Anna said.

"Can we have it?" Ben asked.

They both wanted the balloon. They thought it was pretty and fun. They reached for the string, but it was too high. They jumped, but they could not catch it. They felt sad and frustrated.

Then, they had an idea. They could change something. They could use their backpacks. They took off their backpacks and emptied them. They had some snacks, some water, some books and some toys. They put them on the ground. Then, they tied the backpacks together with the straps. They made a long rope. They threw one end of the rope at the balloon. They missed. They tried again. They missed again. They tried one more time. They got it! They pulled the rope and the balloon came down. They caught the balloon. They felt proud and excited.

"Yay, we did it!" Anna said.

"We changed our backpacks into a rope!" Ben said.

They hugged each other and the balloon. They thanked their backpacks and put their things back inside. They decided to share the balloon and take turns holding it. They walked down the mountain with their mom. They felt happy and grateful. They had a great day at the park.

"Wow, look at the colors!" Tom says. "Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple!"

They enjoy the rainbow for a long time. They make up stories about what is at the end of the rainbow. They pretend they are fairies and unicorns.

"Oh no, where did the rainbow go?" Tom asks. "I want to see it again."

Anna hugs Tom. "Don't be sad," she says. "The rainbow will come back another day. It is the truth. My mom told me."

Tom smiles. "OK, I believe you. You are a good friend."

They hold hands and run to the shelter. They wait for the rain to stop. They hope to see the rainbow again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny gold necklace that she loved to wear every day. One day, she lost her necklace while playing in the park. She was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Her friend, Timmy, saw that she was sad and asked her what was wrong. Lily told him that she lost her gold necklace and couldn't find it. Timmy said, "Don't be sad, I will help you find it. Where did you last have it?"

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their ball. They saw an elderly lady sitting on a bench. She looked sad and lonely. Lily and Tom wanted to make her happy, so they ran to her and offered her their ball.

The elderly lady smiled and thanked them. She said she liked their ball very much. She asked them if they wanted to hear a story. Lily and Tom nodded. They liked stories.

The elderly lady told them a story about a word that could make anything happen. She said the word was very powerful and secret. She said she would tell them the word if they promised to keep it to themselves. Lily and Tom promised. They were curious and excited.

The elderly lady whispered the word in their ears. It was a strange and scary word. Lily and Tom felt a shiver down their spines. They repeated the word after her. Suddenly, the sky turned dark and stormy. The wind howled and the thunder roared. The park was filled with shadows and monsters. Lily and Tom screamed and dropped their ball. They wanted to run away, but they couldn't move. They were stuck to the bench.

The elderly lady laughed wickedly. She said she had tricked them. She said the word was a curse that made their worst fears come true. She said she was a witch who liked to make children suffer. She said she would keep their ball and their souls. She said they would never see their parents or their home again. Lily and Tom cried and begged for mercy, but the elderly lady ignored them. She took their ball and flew away on her broomstick, leaving them alone in the dark and the horror.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and draw with crayons. One day, they find a big box of oats in the kitchen. They think oats are yummy and fun to play with.

"Let's make a picture with oats!" Sara says. She takes some oats and puts them on a paper. She makes a circle for a sun and some lines for rays.

"I want to make a picture too!" Tom says. He takes some oats and puts them on another paper. He makes a square for a house and some dots for windows.

Sara and Tom are happy with their pictures. They show them to each other.

"Look at my sun! It is bright and warm!" Sara says.

"Look at my house! It is big and cozy!" Tom says.

"Hey, what are you doing?" Tom asks. He sees Sara marking on her paper. He thinks she is ruining her picture.

She tries to get the crayon back, but Tom pushes her away.

They start to fight and cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the kitchen. She sees the oats, the papers, the crayon, and the children.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. She is surprised and worried.

She picks up Sara and Tom and hugs them.

"Tell me what happened," Mom says. She is calm and gentle.

Sara and Tom tell Mom their story. They say they are sorry and they love each other.

Mom smiles and kisses them.

"It's okay, my darlings. You can make pictures with oats and crayons, but you have to share and be nice. Oats and crayons are not only for you, they are for everyone. Can you do that?" Mom says.

Sara and Tom nod and hug.

"Yes, Mom. We can do that," Sara and Tom say.

Mom gives them some cookies and milk. They eat and drink and laugh.

They are friends again.

Sara and Ben are twins. They share a room and a big mattress. They like to play and read books before bedtime. But sometimes they hear unusual noises at night. They wonder what makes the noises.

"Hello, mouse," Sara says softly. "Are you hungry?"

The mouse stops and looks at Sara and Ben. It nods and squeaks. It seems friendly.

"Can we be your friends?" Ben asks. "We have more cheese in the kitchen."

The mouse smiles and nods again. It follows Sara and Ben to the kitchen. They give it some cheese and crackers. They play with it for a while. They name it Mimi.

Sara and Ben are happy. They have a new friend. They take Mimi back to their room and make a cozy bed for it under the mattress. They say good night and fall asleep. They do not hear any more unusual noises. They dream of cheese and crackers and Mimi.

Sara and Ben were twins who loved to play hide and seek. One day, they decided to play in their big bedroom, where there were many things to hide behind. Sara was the seeker, and Ben was the hider. Sara counted to ten, and then opened her eyes. She was enthusiastic to find her brother.

She searched under the bed, but Ben was not there. She searched behind the curtains, but Ben was not there. She searched in the closet, but Ben was not there. She searched everywhere, but she could not find Ben. She started to feel sad and worried. Where was Ben?

She heard a giggle from behind the sofa. She ran to the sofa and lifted the pillow that was on the floor. There was Ben, hiding under the pillow. He smiled and said, "You found me, Sara! That was a good hiding spot, right?"

Sara was happy to see Ben, but she was also a little angry. She said, "Ben, that was not fair. You hid under the pillow, and pillows are not for hiding. Pillows are for sleeping and cuddling. You could have hurt the pillow, or made it dirty. And you made me scared, because I thought you were lost. Next time, please hide in a better place, OK?"

Ben felt sorry for what he did. He said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I didn't mean to make you scared, or hurt the pillow. I just wanted to have fun. You're right, pillows are not for hiding. Next time, I will hide in a better place, OK?"

Sara hugged Ben and said, "It's OK, Ben. I forgive you. You're my brother, and I love you. Let's play again, but this time, let's be more careful, OK?"

Ben hugged Sara back and said, "I love you too, Sara. Let's play again, but this time, let's be more careful, OK?"

The twins put the pillow back on the sofa, and started a new game of hide and seek. They had fun, but they also learned to respect their things, and each other's feelings. That was the moral of their story.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big hill with a lot of flowers and grass. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run on the grass. They saw a big yellow truck with a loud horn. It was carrying many boxes and bags.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Lily said. "I wonder what is inside."

"Maybe toys or candy or books," Ben said. "Do you think we can see?"

They ran after the truck, but it was too fast. They stopped at the corner and watched it turn. They saw a sign that said "Happy Birthday, Sam!"

"Who is Sam?" Lily asked. "Do you know him?"

"No, I don't," Ben said. "But he is very lucky. He will get a big surprise."

They decided to follow the truck and find out where Sam lived. They walked and walked until they came to a small house with a modest garden. The truck parked in front of the house and the driver got out. He knocked on the door and a woman opened it.

"Hello, I have a delivery for Sam," the driver said. "Is he home?"

"Yes, he is," the woman said. "He is in his room. He doesn't know anything about this. It's a secret."

The driver smiled and said, "Well, he is in for a big surprise. Can you help me carry these boxes and bags inside?"

The woman nodded and said, "Of course. Thank you so much. Come on, let's go."

Lily and Ben hid behind a bush and watched. They saw the driver and the woman bring many boxes and bags into the house. They heard them whisper and laugh. They wondered what was inside.

"Maybe we can sneak in and see," Lily said. "I'm very curious."

"Me too," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. We don't want to spoil the surprise."

They waited until the driver and the woman left the house. Then they tiptoed to the door and opened it. They saw a big banner that said "Happy Birthday, Sam!" and balloons and streamers and cake and candles. They saw a pile of boxes and bags with bows and tags. They saw a boy sitting on the couch with a big smile on his face.

"Hi, I'm Sam," the boy said. "Who are you?"

Lily and Ben were shocked. They didn't know what to say. They had followed the wrong truck. They had crashed the wrong party. They had met the wrong Sam.

They looked at each other and said, "Oops!"

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a hidden motorcycle in the bushes near their house. It was big and shiny and had two wheels.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "Can we ride it?"

"I don't know," Lily said. "It's not ours. Maybe someone is looking for it."

Tom did not care. He wanted to have fun. He climbed on the motorcycle and pushed a button. It made a loud noise and started to move.

The police officer came and talked to Tom. He was not angry, but he was serious. He told Tom that he did something wrong. He took someone else's motorcycle without asking. He drove it on the road without a helmet or a license. He put himself and others in danger.

Tom felt ashamed and sad. He said he was sorry. He did not mean to do anything bad. He just wanted to have fun.

The police officer nodded and smiled. He said he understood. He said he was glad that Tom was safe and that he stopped. He said he would take the motorcycle back to its owner. He said he would not punish Tom, but he would talk to his parents.

Tom thanked the police officer. He hugged Lily and said he was sorry to her too. He said he would not do it again. He said he learned his lesson.

Lily hugged him back and said she forgave him. She said she loved him. She said they would go home and play with their own toys.

The end.

Anna does not want to bathe her knee. She is afraid of the water and the soap. She thinks they will sting and make her cry. She shakes her head and holds her knee.

"No, no, no," she says. "I don't want to bathe. I want to go home."

Miss Lee is kind and gentle. She takes Anna to the nurse's office. There, she shows her a big tub of warm water and a soft cloth. She also has a band-aid with a picture of a bunny on it.

"Thank you, Miss Lee," she says. "You are a nice teacher. And I like the bunny band-aid. It makes me happy."

"You are very welcome, Anna," says Miss Lee. "I am glad you are happy. And I am proud of you for bathing your knee. You did a great job."

"Can we pet the rabbit?" Anna asked Ben.

"Maybe, but we have to be very quiet and patient," Ben said. "Rabbits are shy and run away if they hear loud noises or see strangers."

Anna and Ben nodded and crept closer to the rabbit, holding out their hands gently. The rabbit saw them and stopped eating. It looked at them with curious eyes, but did not run away. Anna and Ben smiled and waited for the rabbit to come to them.

After a while, the rabbit hopped closer and sniffed their hands. It felt their fingers with its whiskers and licked them softly. Anna and Ben giggled and stroked the rabbit's fur. The rabbit seemed to like them and let them pet it for a long time.

Anna and Ben were so happy that they forgot about their letter. They played with the rabbit until it was time to go home. Then they said goodbye to the rabbit and thanked it for being their friend. They remembered their letter and ran to the mailbox. They put the letter in the slot and waved to their grandma in their minds.

They learned that if they are patient and kind, they can make new friends and have fun. They also learned that they should not forget their promises and duties, even when they are having fun. They hoped that their grandma would like their letter and be proud of them.

Ben and Mia went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But Ben and Mia liked the fish best. They ran to the big glass tank, where they could see the fish swim.

"Look, look!" Mia said. "There is a big octopus! It has eight legs and a round head. It is purple and green. It is so pretty!"

Ben nodded. He wanted to touch the octopus. He put his hand on the glass. He hoped the octopus would come closer. But the octopus did not see him. It swam away to the other side of the tank.

"Come back, octopus!" Ben said. "I want to be your friend. I want to play with you."

Mia shook her head. She knew the octopus could not hear Ben. She also knew the octopus could not get out of the tank. She tried to explain to Ben.

"Ben, you cannot play with the octopus. The octopus lives in the water. You live on the land. The octopus needs the water to breathe. You need the air to breathe. The octopus is happy in the tank. It has food and space and other fish."

Ben frowned. He did not understand. He still wanted to play with the octopus. He looked at the tank. He saw a wide hole at the top. He had an idea.

"Maybe I can get the octopus out of the hole," he said. "Then I can hold it and hug it and take it home."

Mia gasped. She knew that was a bad idea. She grabbed Ben's arm.

"No, Ben, no!" she said. "You cannot do that. That is not nice. That is not safe. The octopus will be scared and hurt. You will be wet and cold. Mom and Dad will be mad. The zoo people will be sad. Please, Ben, leave the octopus alone. Let it be."

Ben looked at Mia. He saw her eyes were big and worried. He saw her mouth was tight and serious. He felt her hand was warm and strong. He thought about what she said. He did not want to scare or hurt the octopus. He did not want to be wet or cold. He did not want to make Mom and Dad mad or the zoo people sad. He wanted to be nice and safe. He wanted to make Mia happy. He let go of the glass. He smiled at Mia.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big tent with a zipper. It was green and yellow. It looked mysterious.

"Who lives in the tent?" Sara asked.

"I don't know. Maybe a clown or a magician," Ben said.

"Can we go inside and see?" Sara said.

Ben was not sure. He looked around. He did not see anyone near the tent.

"OK, but we have to be quiet and careful," he said.

They walked to the tent. They pulled the zipper. It made a loud noise. They opened the tent. They saw a lot of toys and books. They also saw a big dog. It was brown and white. It had a red collar. It barked at them.

"Wow, look at all the stuff!" Sara said.

"Shh, the dog might bite us!" Ben said.

They heard a voice. It was a woman. She sounded angry.

"Hey, what are you doing in my tent? Get out of here!" she said.

She came out of the tent. She had long hair and a hat. She looked like a hippie.

"Sorry, we were just curious," Sara said.

"Yeah, we didn't mean to bother you," Ben said.

They ran out of the tent. They ran back to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She had a book and a sandwich.

"Mom, we saw a mysterious tent and a big dog and a hippie lady!" Sara said.

"Really? That sounds exciting. But you shouldn't go into other people's tents without permission. That's rude and dangerous," mom said.

She hugged them and gave them a bite of her sandwich.

"We know, mom. We're sorry. We won't do it again," Ben said.

Mom smiled and kissed them.

"I love you, my little adventurers. You remind me of myself when I was young," she said.

Ben and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Ben found a bottle of oil and poured some into a big pan. He said, "I will make a yummy cake with oil and flour and sugar."

Mia saw the oil and said, "No, Ben, oil is not for cakes. Oil is for cars and machines. It will make the cake taste bad and make us sick." She tried to take the bottle from Ben, but he held it tight.

They started to fight over the bottle. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The bottle slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. The oil spilled everywhere. It made the floor slippery and shiny.

Ben and Mia slipped and slid on the oil. They could not stand up or walk. They felt uncomfortable and scared. They cried for help.

Mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the mess and was angry. She said, "What have you done? You have wasted the oil and made the kitchen dirty. You are in big trouble." She slapped her hand on the table to show how mad she was.

Ben and Mia heard the slap and felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing and we did not mean to spill the oil. Please help us get up and clean the kitchen."

Mom sighed and said, "Okay, I will help you, but you have to promise me to never play with oil again. Oil is not a toy. It is dangerous and wasteful. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nodded and said, "We understand, Mom. We promise to never play with oil again. We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Ben and Mia. Now let's get you out of this oily mess." She took their hands and helped them stand up. She gave them a hug and a kiss and said, "Next time, if you want to make a cake, ask me first. I will show you how to use the right ingredients and tools."

Ben and Mia said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom. You are the best chef in the world."

One day, a raven saw a farmer work in his field. The raven was hungry and wanted to eat some of the farmer's corn. He flew down and landed on a scarecrow. He thought the scarecrow was a real person and said, "Hello, friend. Can I have some of your corn?"

The scarecrow did not answer, because it was not alive. The raven thought the scarecrow was rude and said, "Fine, then I will take some anyway." He pecked at the corn and filled his beak. He was about to fly away when he heard a loud noise. It was the farmer, who had seen the raven and shouted, "Hey, you! Stop stealing my corn!"

The raven was scared and tried to fly away, but his beak was too full. He dropped some of the corn and flew faster. The farmer ran after him and threw a stick at him. The stick hit the raven's wing and made him fall to the ground. The farmer caught the raven and said, "You are a bad bird. You should not take what is not yours. You should work for your food, like I do."

The raven felt sorry and said, "Please, let me go. I will not do it again. I will work for my food, like you do." The farmer looked at the raven and said, "How will you work for your food? You are a bird, not a farmer."

The raven thought for a moment and said, "I can sing for you. I have a beautiful voice. I can make you happy with my songs." The farmer smiled and said, "That is a good idea. You can sing for me and I will give you some corn. But you must promise to never steal from me again." The raven nodded and said, "I promise. Thank you for being kind to me." The farmer let the raven go and gave him some corn. The raven sang a happy song and flew away.

The moral of the story is: It is better to work for what you want than to steal from others. Stealing can get you into trouble and make you lose friends. Working can make you proud and earn you respect.
