Ben did not like cauliflower. He thought it was white and yucky and smelled bad. He always tried to hide it under his plate or give it to his dog. But his mom knew his tricks and always made him eat it.

One day, mom made a big pot of cauliflower soup for dinner. Ben looked at it and felt sick. He did not want to eat it at all. He wished he could make it disappear.

"Ben, come and eat your soup. It is good for you," mom said.

"No, thank you, mom. I am not hungry," Ben said.

"Yes, you are. You have to eat your soup or you will not get any dessert," mom said.

Ben sighed and went to the table. He looked at his bowl of soup and saw something shiny in it. It was a spoon. He picked it up and saw that it had a button on it. He pressed the button and the spoon made a beep.

"What is that, Ben?" mom asked.

"It is a magic spoon, mom. It can make things disappear," Ben said.

"Really? How does it work?" mom asked.

Ben pointed the spoon at his soup and pressed the button again. The soup vanished from his bowl. Ben smiled.

"See, mom? It works. The soup is gone," Ben said.

Mom looked at his empty bowl and gasped. She did not believe it. She thought Ben was playing a trick on her.

"Ben, where did you get that spoon? And where did the soup go?" mom asked.

"I found it in the soup, mom. And the soup went away. Far, far away," Ben said.

Mom was very confused and worried. She did not know what to do. She wondered if the spoon was dangerous or if Ben was crazy.

"Ben, give me that spoon. It is not a toy. It might be dangerous," mom said.

But Ben did not want to give up his spoon. He liked it. He thought it was fun. He wanted to make more things disappear.

"No, mom. It is mine. I like it. It is fun," Ben said.

He ran away from the table and into his room. He closed the door and locked it. He looked around and saw his toys, his books, his clothes. He pointed the spoon at them and pressed the button. One by one, they all disappeared. Ben laughed and laughed. He thought he was having the best time ever.

But soon, he realized that he had nothing left in his room. He had made everything disappear. He felt lonely and bored. He wished he had his toys, his books, his clothes back. He wished he had not made his soup disappear. He wished he had listened to his mom.

He tried to press the button again, but nothing happened. The spoon was out of power. It could not make things appear. It could only make things disappear.

Ben started to cry. He wanted his mom. He wanted to say sorry. He wanted to hug her. He wanted to eat his soup.

He opened the door and ran to the kitchen. He hoped his mom was still there. He hoped she was not mad at him. He hoped she still loved him.

But when he got to the kitchen, he saw that it was empty. There was no mom. There was no pot. There was no soup. There was nothing.

Ben had made his mom disappear.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with many trees and flowers. One day, they found a bird's nest on a branch. The nest had four blue eggs inside.

"Look, Ben, baby birds!" Anna said, pointing at the nest.

"Can we touch them?" Ben asked, reaching his hand.

"No, Ben, we can't. Mama bird will be sad if we do. She worked hard to make the nest and keep the eggs warm. We have to be kind and leave them alone," Anna said, pulling Ben back.

"Okay, Anna, you are right. Let's go play with our ball instead," Ben said, nodding.

They ran to get their ball and played until it was time for dinner. They ate their soup and bread and drank their milk. Then they brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. Mama and Papa gave them a hug and a kiss and tucked them in their beds.

"Good night, Anna and Ben. Sleep well and have sweet dreams," Mama said.

"Good night, Mama and Papa. We love you," Anna and Ben said.

They closed their eyes and lay in their beds. They listened to the crickets and the wind. They felt cozy and happy. They did not know that something beautiful was going to happen that night.

The next morning, they woke up to a loud chirping sound. They jumped out of their beds and ran to the window. They saw the bird's nest on the branch. But instead of four blue eggs, they saw four baby birds with yellow feathers and black eyes. They were opening their mouths and calling for their mama.

"Wow, Anna, look! The baby birds are here! They hatched last night!" Ben said, clapping his hands.

"They are so cute, Ben! And they are hungry. I hope mama bird comes soon to feed them," Anna said, smiling.

They watched the baby birds for a while, then they got dressed and went downstairs. They told Mama and Papa what they saw. Mama and Papa were proud of them for being kind and respectful to the bird's nest.

"You see, Anna and Ben, sometimes being patient and gentle can bring you wonderful surprises. You helped the baby birds to be born by leaving them alone. And now you can enjoy their beauty and their songs," Mama said.

"Yes, Mama, we understand. We are happy we did the right thing. And we are happy we have each other," Anna and Ben said.

They hugged Mama and Papa and ate their breakfast. Then they went outside to play and to watch the baby birds grow. They learned that night was a special time when magic could happen. And they learned that being kind and caring was the most beautiful thing of all.

Tom and Lily were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and houses with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.

But their baby brother Ben did not like the blocks. He liked to crawl and grab and throw things. He saw the blocks and wanted to play with them too. He crawled to the living room and disturbed Tom and Lily's game.

"Hey, stop that!" Tom shouted. He was angry because Ben knocked down his tower. "You are ruining our game!"

"No, no, no!" Lily cried. She was sad because Ben threw her bridge. "You are breaking our blocks!"

Ben did not understand. He thought they were playing with him. He laughed and clapped his hands. He saw a large block with a zero on it. He liked the zero. He grabbed the block and put it in his mouth.

"Yuck, don't do that!" Tom said. He ran to Ben and took the block from him. "That is not food, that is a block!"

"Give it back, give it back!" Ben whined. He reached for the block and pulled Tom's hair. "That is mine, that is mine!"

Tom and Lily started to cry. They did not like Ben. They wanted him to go away. They called their mom.

"Mom, mom, help!" they said. "Ben is disturbing us! He is taking our blocks and putting them in his mouth!"

Mom heard their cries and came to the living room. She saw the mess and the tears. She felt sorry for Tom and Lily and angry with Ben.

"Ben, what are you doing?" she asked. She took Ben from the floor and held him in her arms. "You are not being nice. You are disturbing your brother and sister. You have to share and play gently with the blocks. Say sorry to Tom and Lily."

Ben looked at Mom and then at Tom and Lily. He saw their sad faces. He felt a little sorry. He said in a small voice, "Sorry, sorry."

Mom smiled and kissed Ben. She said, "That's good, Ben. Now, let's clean up the blocks and play together nicely. OK?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They wiped their tears and smiled too. They said, "OK, OK."

They helped Mom to pick up the blocks and put them in a box. Then they took some blocks and gave them to Ben. They showed him how to stack them and make shapes with them. Ben liked that. He smiled and clapped his hands. He said, "Thank you, thank you."

They played together nicely with the blocks. They did not disturb each other. They had fun. Mom was happy. She said, "Good job, kids. I love you all."

Once upon a time, there were two friends; Jack and Jill. They were both very independent.

Jill came over and said, "Let me help you. I'll carry you."

Jill said, "We need to be careful! We should always stick together so no one has to fall again."

Jack nodded and said, "Yes, that's a good idea".

And so the two friends taught us all a valuable lesson: together we are stronger!

Jenny was very happy. She was going to the palace with her mom and dad. They were going to meet the queen. Jenny loved the queen. She had seen her on TV and in books. She wanted to say hello and give her a hug.

They got to the palace and waited in a big room. There were many other people there. They all wore nice clothes and smiled. Jenny wore a pink dress and a bow in her hair. She felt like a princess. She held her mom's hand and looked around.

Soon, a man came and said it was time to meet the queen. He led them to another room. There was a red carpet and a big chair. The queen was sitting on the chair. She wore a long dress and a shiny crown. She looked very pretty and kind. Jenny was excited.

The man said their names and they walked up to the queen. Jenny's mom and dad bowed and said hello. The queen smiled and nodded. Then she looked at Jenny. Jenny smiled and said, "Hi, queen. I'm Jenny. I'm very happy to meet you. You are very pretty and nice. Can I give you a hug?"

The queen was surprised. She was not used to children talking to her like that. She did not like hugs. She thought they were messy and rude. She frowned and said, "No, you can't. You are a very naughty girl. You should not talk to me like that. You should be quiet and respectful. Go away. You are not welcome here."

Jenny was shocked. She did not understand. She had only wanted to be friendly. She felt sad and scared. She started to cry. Her mom and dad were also shocked. They tried to apologize and comfort Jenny. They said they were sorry and they loved her. They wanted to leave.

But the queen was angry. She did not accept their apology. She said they had offended her. She said they had to be punished. She called her guards and told them to take them away. She said they had to go to the dungeon. She said they would never see the sun again.

The guards grabbed Jenny and her mom and dad. They dragged them out of the room. They did not listen to their pleas and cries. They took them to a dark and cold place. They locked them in a cell. They left them alone.

Jenny and her mom and dad hugged each other. They were very sad and afraid. They did not know what would happen to them. They wished they had never come to the palace. They wished they had never met the queen. They wished they had stayed home and had a delicious cake.

At the park, they saw a big tree. Under the tree, there was a box. Sue said, "Tom, let's open the box and see what's inside." Tom said, "Okay, let's do it!" They opened the box and saw a note. The note said, "Find the hidden toy and you will win an incredible prize."

Sue and Tom searched and searched. They looked under rocks, behind bushes, and in the sandbox. Finally, they found the hidden toy. It was a small, red car. They were so happy!

They went back to the big tree with the toy. They waited and waited for their incredible prize. But no prize came. Sue and Tom were sad. They didn't understand why they didn't win the incredible prize.

As the sun went down, they went home with the small, red car. They didn't get the incredible prize they wanted, but they still had fun playing together.

Lily was playing with her doll in her room. She liked to pretend that her doll was a princess and she was her friend. She had a small box that she used as a treasure chest. She put a shiny key inside the box and locked it. She said to her doll, "This is our secret. No one can open the box without the key."

But then she heard a loud sneeze from the hallway. It was her brother, Max. He had a cold and he was looking for a tissue. He saw Lily's door open and he walked in. He saw the box on the floor and he was curious. He picked it up and shook it. He heard something rattle inside. He said, "What is this? What is in here?"

Lily saw Max with her box and she was angry. She ran to him and tried to grab the box. She said, "No, Max, that is mine! That is my treasure! Give it back!" But Max was bigger and stronger. He held the box high above his head. He said, "No, Lily, this is mine now. I want to see what is in here. Maybe it is something cool."

Lily started to cry. She said, "Please, Max, please. That is my key. That is my special key. I need it for my doll. She is a princess and she needs her key." But Max did not listen. He tried to open the box with his fingers. But the lock was too tight. He said, "This is a stupid box. It does not open. I need something to break it."

He looked around the room and he saw a pair of scissors on the desk. He said, "Aha, I found it. I will use this to open the box." He ran to the desk and grabbed the scissors. He was about to cut the box when he heard a voice behind him. It was Mom. She said, "Max, what are you doing? Put down those scissors. They are not available for you. They are dangerous. And why are you holding Lily's box? Did you ask her if you can play with it?"

Max turned around and saw Mom. He felt scared and guilty. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I just wanted to see what was in the box. Lily said it was her treasure and she had a key. I wanted to see the key." Mom said, "Well, you should have asked her nicely. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not use scissors to open things. You could hurt yourself or the box. Now, give the box back to Lily and say you are sorry."

Max gave the box back to Lily and said he was sorry. Lily hugged the box and said thank you. She opened the box with her key and showed Max the key. She said, "This is my key. It is shiny and pretty. It is for my doll. She is a princess and she needs her key." Max said, "Wow, that is a nice key. Can I see it?" Lily said, "Yes, you can see it. But you have to be gentle and careful. And you have to ask me first." Max said, "OK, I will. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister." Lily said, "You are welcome, Max. You are a good brother. But you need a tissue. You still have a cold. Come on, let's go find one." They both smiled and walked out of the room. Mom followed them and said, "That's better. I'm proud of you both. Now, let's get some juice and cookies. They are available in the kitchen." They all went to the kitchen and had a snack. They were happy and they forgot about the sneeze.

"Jen, how did you do that?" Tom asks.

"I was nice to the dog," Jen says. "He was not mean. He was just scared. You have to work with dogs, not run from them."

Tom nods. He feels sorry for running away. He wants to be brave like Jen. He walks to the dog. He pets the dog. The dog wags his tail again.

Tom and Jen smile. They have a new friend. They learn that dogs are not bad. They learn that work and stay are better than run and hide. They learn to be kind and brave.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had many toys and flowers to have fun with. But there was one plant that they did not like. It was ugly and prickly and had no colors. They always ignored it and never watered it or touched it.

One day, a fairy came to visit the garden. She saw the ugly plant and felt sorry for it. She flew over to it and said, "Hello, little plant. Why are you so sad and lonely?"

The plant looked up and saw the fairy. It was surprised and happy. It said, "Hello, fairy. I am sad and lonely because no one likes me. Ben and Lily ignore me and never play with me. They say I am ugly and prickly and have no colors."

The fairy smiled and said, "That is not true. You are not ugly, you are special. You are prickly because you are strong and can protect yourself. You have no colors because you are waiting for the right time to bloom. I like you and I want to be your friend."

The fairy gave the plant a hug and a kiss. She sprinkled some magic dust on it and said, "I have a gift for you. Tomorrow, you will have the most beautiful flowers in the garden. Then Ben and Lily will see how wonderful you are and they will want to play with you too."

The plant thanked the fairy and felt very happy. The fairy flew away and said, "Goodbye, little plant. See you tomorrow."

The next day, Ben and Lily came to the garden. They saw the ugly plant and gasped. It was not ugly anymore. It had big and bright flowers of many colors. It smelled sweet and looked happy. Ben and Lily ran over to it and said, "Wow, what a beautiful plant! How did this happen? Can we play with you?"

The plant smiled and said, "Yes, you can play with me. I am happy to have new friends. But please do not ignore me again. I was lonely and sad before. A fairy came and helped me. She said I was special and gave me these flowers. She also said you should be kind and gentle to all plants, even if they look different."

Ben and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry, plant. We were wrong to ignore you and call you ugly. You are special and beautiful. We want to be your friends too. Can you forgive us?"

The plant nodded and said, "Yes, I forgive you. You are also special and beautiful. Let's be friends and have fun together."

Ben and Lily hugged the plant and said, "Thank you, plant. Thank you, fairy. We have learned a lesson today. We will never judge a plant by its looks again. We will love and care for all plants in the garden."

They played with the plant and the other flowers. They had a lot of fun and laughter. The plant was happy and grateful. The fairy watched them from afar and smiled. She was proud and glad. She had done a good deed.

One day, their mom made a big steak for dinner. She also made some carrots and peas. She told Ben and Sam to eat everything on their plates. But Ben and Sam only ate the steak and drank the juice. They left the carrots and peas untouched.

"Mom, can we have more steak and juice?" they asked.

"No, you can't," mom said. "You have to eat your vegetables too. They are good for you. They make you strong and healthy."

"But we are not hungry for vegetables," Ben and Sam said. "We are hungry for steak and juice."

Mom shook her head. She was not happy. She said, "If you don't eat your vegetables, you will not grow well. You will get sick and tired. And you will not have any dessert."

Ben and Sam did not listen. They did not care. They threw away their vegetables and went to play.

The next day, Ben and Sam woke up feeling sick. They had a fever and a stomach ache. They could not play or have fun. They had to stay in bed and drink water.

Mom came to check on them. She said, "I told you to eat your vegetables. But you did not listen. Now you are sick. You have to eat better and listen to me. I know what is good for you."

Ben and Sam felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. You are right. We should have eaten our vegetables. We will eat them next time. Please forgive us."

Mom smiled. She said, "I forgive you. I love you. I hope you get well soon. And I have a surprise for you. I made some cookies for dessert. But you can only have them if you eat your vegetables first."

Ben and Sam nodded. They said, "We will, mom. We will. Thank you for the cookies. And thank you for taking care of us."

The moral of the story is: You should eat your vegetables and listen to your mom. She knows what is good for you.

Mom hugged Jen and Tom. She was angry and relieved. She scolded Tom for being foolish and praised Jen for being brave. She said they should always keep their promises and stay away from the pit.

Tom learned his lesson. He said sorry to Jen and Mom. He said he would never lie again. He said he would be more careful and smart. He said he would listen to Jen and Mom. He said he loved them.

Jen forgave Tom. She said she was glad he was okay. She said she would always help him. She said she loved him.

They hugged and kissed. They were happy and safe. They were brother and sister.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have a big rug with roads and buildings on it. They make sounds like vroom and beep as they drive their cars around. Sometimes they have races or pretend to go to the shop or the park.

One day, Anna and Ben have a problem. They both want to play with the same car. It is a red car with a shiny sticker on it. They think it is the coolest car ever. They both reach for it at the same time and pull on it.

"Let go, it's mine!" Anna says.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says.

They tug and tug until the car breaks in half. They both gasp and drop the pieces. They feel sad and angry.

"Look what you did!" Anna says.

"You did it!" Ben says.

They start to cry and yell at each other. Their mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken car and the upset children.

"What happened here?" she asks.

They both point at each other and say, "He/she did it!"

Mom sighs and picks up the pieces of the car. She looks at them and says, "I think I can fix this. But first, you two need to calm down and say sorry to each other. How about you do some exercise to get rid of your bad feelings?"

Anna and Ben nod. They don't like to fight. Mom shows them how to do some jumping jacks, some squats, and some stretches. They follow her and start to feel better. They breathe deeply and smile.

"Are you ready to say sorry now?" Mom asks.

Anna and Ben look at each other and say, "Sorry."

They hug and say, "I love you."

Mom smiles and says, "I love you too. And I have good news. I fixed your car. See, it can still drive and reverse. And the sticker is still cool. But you have to share it and be gentle with it, okay?"

Anna and Ben nod and say, "Okay."

They take the car and thank Mom. They go back to their rug and play nicely. They take turns driving and reversing the car. They make sounds like vroom and beep. They are happy again.

"Yes, mom. But we don't want to sleep in our camp anymore. It's too weird." Sam said.

"Can we sleep in our beds, please?" Ben asked.

"Of course, you can. Come on, let's go inside. It's time to end your camp adventure." their dad said.

They gathered some sticks and lit a fire. Soon, they were all warm and cozy inside their brick house. Peppa was so happy that they found an easy solution to their problem. From then on, they always made sure to have a fire when it got cold outside. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play her piano every day. But one day, her piano stopped working. Lily tried to fix it, but she couldn't. She was very sad because she loved her piano so much.

Lily's mom knew how much the piano meant to her. So, she decided to get a new one for her. They went to the music store and found a beautiful piano. The man at the store said it was very dependable and would last a long time.

Lily was so happy when she saw her new piano. She played it all day and all night. She was no longer sad and her music sounded even better on her new piano. She knew she could always depend on it to work.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little creature. It loved to walk in the nature. Every day, the creature would explore the world around it. It enjoyed taking long walks through the woods, looking at the trees, the flowers and birds.

On one sunny day, the creature decided to go on a special adventure. It put on its most comfortable shoes and set off! Soon, it was surrounded by beautiful nature. It jumped over logs, climbed tall trees, and listened to the singing of the birds.

The creature soon saw a lovely meadow filled with bright yellow flowers. So, it ran through the meadow and spun around with its arms wide open. The air was fresh, the sun was warm and the creature felt very jolly.

After a few hours of exploring, it was time to go home. But the creature knew it would come back soon. After all, it had found a new friend in the nature!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Bob. Bob wanted to win a race. Every day he practiced running, jumping and hopping. One day, the race day came. 

Bob was nervous but he tried to be brave. He lined up with the other kids. When the race began Bob ran as fast as he could. He beat the other kids and was first to the finish line. Everyone cheered for him!

Bob felt so happy to win the race. He was so pleased that he shouted out loud. He enjoyed being the winner and laughed as he ran back to his Mom.

The next day, he had to compete against the other kids again. This time, Bob finished last. He was sad and felt terrible. 

But then his mom told him it was okay; being brave and trying his best was more important than winning. Bob smiled and knew that he could still enjoy the race, even if he didn't win.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sara. She was three years old and loved to play on the playground. Every day, she went to the playground and played on the slide.

One day when she was playing, her mom called her. "Sara, time to go home!", her mom said. But Sara refused to go home. She wanted to keep playing on the slide.

"Mommy, please! I don't want to go home!", said Sara.

"OK, one more turn on the slide and then you have to go home," said her mom. Sara agreed and went down the slide one last time.

When she got to the bottom, she was sorry. She wished she had stayed and played a little bit longer. But her mom said it was time to go home.

Sara hugged her mom and said goodbye to the slide. She learned that it was sometimes important to listen to your mom.

One day, when Jack was playing in the garden, he saw a silly rabbit hopping from bush to bush. Jack thought it was very funny and he started to giggle. 

The rabbit then said, "Stop laughing! Don't be so stupid!" Jack replied, "I'm not being stupid, I'm just having fun!" 

The rabbit then said, "Let's make a deal. If you shake this wool, it will grow longer and I can use it to make a nice warm home. What do you say?" 

Jack thought it was a great idea, so he picked up the wool and started to shake it vigorously. After a while, the wool got longer and longer and the rabbit was so happy! It was a perfect home to live in. 

Jack had a lot of fun that day and he also learned a valuable lesson. He learned that being silly can sometimes lead to great things.

Bella the squirrel was very sleepy. She had been playing all day with her friends in the forest. She wanted to go to her nest and take a nap, but she had one more thing to do. She had to find an acorn for her mom.

She looked around the trees and the ground, but she could not see any acorns. She yawned and rubbed her eyes. She was too tired to keep looking. She saw a big oak tree with a hole in it. Maybe there was an acorn inside, she thought.

She climbed up the tree and peeked into the hole. She saw a shiny brown acorn. She reached in and grabbed it. She was about to leave when she heard a voice.

"Hey, that's my acorn!" It was Sammy the chipmunk. He lived in the hole with his family. He looked angry and sad.

Bella felt guilty. She knew she had done something bad. She did not want to make Sammy cry. She said, "I'm sorry, Sammy. I did not know it was your acorn. I was looking for one for my mom. I'm very sleepy and I wanted to go home."

Sammy looked at Bella. He saw that she was sorry and sleepy. He said, "It's okay, Bella. I have more acorns in my hole. You can have this one for your mom. But next time, please ask before you take something that is not yours."

Bella smiled and thanked Sammy. She said, "You are very kind, Sammy. I will ask next time. I hope you have a good nap." She took the acorn and climbed down the tree. She ran to her nest and gave the acorn to her mom. Her mom hugged her and said, "You are a good squirrel, Bella. I'm proud of you." Bella snuggled with her mom and fell asleep. She dreamed of acorns and friends.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big hole in the ground. It was a well. They wanted to look inside.

"Can we enter the well?" Lily asked Tom.

"No, it is too deep and dark. We might fall and get hurt," Tom said.

"But I want to see what is in there. Maybe there are fish or frogs or coins," Lily said.

She tried to climb on the edge of the well, but Tom pulled her back.

"Stop, Lily! It is not safe. We can play with something else," Tom said.

Lily was frustrated. She did not like Tom telling her what to do. She pushed him away and ran to the well. She leaned over and shouted.

"Hello, well! Can you hear me?"

She waited for an answer, but there was only silence. She shouted louder.

"Hello, well! Are you there?"

She still heard nothing. She was disappointed. She thought the well would be fun and exciting, but it was boring and empty.

She turned around and saw Tom. He was holding a ball and a rope. He smiled at her.

"Come on, Lily. Let's play with this. We can throw the ball and catch it with the rope. It will be more fun than the well," he said.

Lily looked at the ball and the rope. They looked bright and colorful. She felt curious and happy. She forgot about the well.

"Okay, Tom. Let's play with that," she said.

She ran to him and took the rope. They threw the ball and caught it with the rope. They laughed and had fun. They did not enter the well. They played in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in the jungle. He loved to roar and scare his animal friends. One day, he went for a walk in the bush and met a little rabbit. The rabbit was scared of the lion's roar and asked him why he was so loud. The lion said, "I roar because it's fun and it makes me feel strong."

The rabbit asked the lion if he could play with him, but the lion said he was too busy. The rabbit was sad, but then he saw a bunch of carrots in the bush. He realized that it's important to make time for friends and that sometimes, the best things are available in the simplest places. From that day on, the lion and the rabbit played together in the bush and the lion roared only when they were playing a game.

"Let's go, Tom!" Anna said. "Maybe we can find something fun!"

"Thank you, lady!" Anna said. "You are very nice and sweet!"

They hugged the old lady and said goodbye. They walked back to the park and continued to play. They were happy and grateful. They had a wonderful day.

Lily was a girl who liked to draw. She had many colors and papers to make pictures. She wanted to draw a flower for her mom. She looked out the window and saw a red flower in the garden. She thought it was pretty and wanted to draw it.

She took her colors and papers and went outside. She found the red flower and sat down next to it. She looked at it carefully and started to draw. She used red and green and yellow. She tried to make the flower look like the one in the garden.

But she had a problem. Her colors were not sharp. They were dull and broken. She could not make the lines and shapes she wanted. She was sad and frustrated. She did not know what to do.

She heard a voice behind her. It was her dad. He saw her drawing and smiled. He said, "What are you doing, Lily?"

He showed her how to use the sharpener. He put a color in the hole and turned it. The sharpener made a noise and shaved off the dull part of the color. He took out the color and showed it to Lily. It was sharp and bright. He said, "See? Now you can draw better."

Lily was amazed and happy. She said, "Wow! Thank you, dad. Can I try?"

He hugged her and said, "You are a great artist, Lily. And a great daughter. I'm very proud of you."

Lily hugged him back and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you. And I love mom. And I love the flower."

They went inside and gave the drawing to mom. Mom was very happy and thanked Lily. She said, "This is the best gift ever, Lily. You are very sweet and talented. I love you very much."

They all hugged and kissed and smiled. They were a happy family. And the flower in the garden smiled too.

Lily and Sam were twins. They liked to play together in the park. One day, their mom said they could have ice-cream if they were good. Lily and Sam were very happy.

They ran to the ice-cream truck and waited in line. Lily wanted a pink ice-cream and Sam wanted a blue one. They held their mom's hand and said please and thank you to the ice-cream man.

Mom gave them a napkin and said, "Be careful, don't drop your ice-cream. It will melt in the sun. Stay close to me and don't run away."

Lily and Sam nodded and licked their ice-creams. They were very yummy. They saw some birds and flowers and swings. They wanted to see them more.

"Mom, can we go there?" Lily asked, pointing to the swings.

"Not now, sweetie. We have to finish our ice-creams first. They will make a mess if we move too much." Mom said.

"But I want to swing!" Sam said, pouting.

"Me too!" Lily said.

They looked at their ice-creams. They were still big and cold. They looked at the swings. They were empty and fun.

They had an idea. They put their ice-creams on the ground and ran to the swings. They forgot what mom said. They thought they would be back soon.

Mom saw them and called, "Lily! Sam! Come back! Where are you going? Don't leave your ice-creams!"

But Lily and Sam did not hear her. They were too busy swinging. They laughed and shouted and pushed each other. They had a lot of fun.

But they did not see what happened to their ice-creams. The sun was hot and the ice-creams were not. They melted and dripped and made a puddle. Some ants and flies came and ate them. Some dogs and cats came and licked them. Some kids and adults came and stepped on them.

When Lily and Sam were tired of swinging, they remembered their ice-creams. They ran back to where they left them. But they did not find them. They only found a mess.

They looked at each other and felt sad. They had no ice-creams. They had no napkins. They had no mom.

They started to cry. They wanted their ice-creams. They wanted their mom.

Mom heard them and came to them. She saw the mess and felt angry. She said, "Lily! Sam! What did you do? I told you to stay with me and not to drop your ice-creams. Look what happened. They are gone. You wasted them. You disobeyed me. You made me worry. I am not proud of you."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too, Lily and Sam. But you have to listen to me and do what I say. I know what is best for you. I want you to be safe and happy and good. Next time, stay with me and finish your ice-creams. Then we can go to the swings. OK?"

Lily and Sam nodded and said, "OK, mom. We will do that. We will be good. We will make you proud."

Mom smiled and said, "That's my twins. Come on, let's go home and clean up. Maybe we can have some more ice-cream later. But only if you are good."

Lily and Sam smiled and said, "Yes, mom. We will be good. We love ice-cream. We love you more."

Ben and Mia like to play with snow. They make snowballs and snowmen and snow forts. They have fun in the cold.

"Maybe it is a snake," Ben says.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben says. He drops the wire. It burns his hand.

Ben and Mia nod. They say, "Yes, mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will not touch the wire again."

Mom smiles. She says, "It's okay. You are curious and creative. But you have to be careful and safe. There are many other things you can play with in the snow. How about we make some hot chocolate and cookies?"

Ben and Lily were playing in the yard. They saw a big pile of leaves that their dad had raked. They wanted to jump in the leaves and have fun.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "The leaves are dry and soft. We can make a big mess!"

"No, Ben," Lily said. "Dad worked hard to rake the leaves. He told us to help him fold the bags and put the leaves inside. If we jump in the leaves, we will make more work for him."

"But it's boring to fold bags," Ben said. "It's fun to jump in leaves. Come on, Lily, don't be a baby."

Ben ran to the pile and jumped in. He laughed and threw leaves in the air. Lily watched him and felt sad. She knew dad would be angry when he saw the mess.

She went to the garage and got a rake. She started to rake the leaves back into the pile. She worked hard and did not stop.

Soon, dad came back from the store. He saw Ben in the leaves and Lily with the rake. He was not happy.

"Ben, what are you doing?" he asked. "You made a big mess of the leaves. You did not listen to me or help me. You were selfish and lazy."

He saw Lily and smiled. "Lily, thank you for raking the leaves. You listened to me and helped me. You were kind and helpful."

He gave Lily a hug and a cookie. He told Ben to get out of the leaves and fold the bags. Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Lily and dad.

The moral of the story is: It is better to be helpful and kind than selfish and lazy.

Sara tells her mom about the bird. Her mom is proud of Sara for being kind and brave. She says, "You are a good veterinarian, Sara. But we need to take the bird to a real veterinarian. They have special tools and medicine to fix the bird's wing."

Sara nods and agrees. She says, "Can I come with you, mom? I want to see how they help the bird."

Sara shows her the bird and tells her what happened. Dr. Lee smiles and says, "You are a very good veterinarian, Sara. You did the right thing to bring the bird here. Let me take a look at it and see what I can do."

Sara thinks for a moment and says, "I want to name it Sunny. Because it has yellow feathers and it makes me happy."

Lily and Ben were playing in their room. They liked to pretend they were in different places. Sometimes they were pirates, sometimes they were astronauts, sometimes they were fairies.

Today they wanted to be kings and queens. They looked for some clothes to wear in their wardrobe. They found a big red cloak, a shiny crown, a long blue dress and a furry cape. They put them on and felt very royal.

"Let's go to our castle," said Lily. "We can have a tea party with our friends."

"OK," said Ben. "But who will we include in our tea party?"

Lily thought for a moment. She looked around the room and saw her teddy bear, her doll, her robot and her book. She smiled and said, "We can include all of them. They are our loyal subjects."

Ben nodded and said, "That sounds fun. Let's go."

They picked up their toys and carried them to their castle. Their castle was a big cardboard box that their dad had brought home. It had windows and a door and a flag on top. They put their toys inside and sat down on some pillows.

They pretended to pour tea from a plastic pot and eat cookies from a paper plate. They talked to their toys and asked them how they were. They had a lot of fun.

But then they heard their mom calling them. "Lily, Ben, it's time for lunch. Come downstairs, please."

They looked at each other and sighed. They didn't want to leave their castle. They wanted to play more.

"Can we come back later?" asked Lily.

"Of course," said Ben. "Our castle will be here. And our toys will be dry and warm in the wardrobe."

They took off their clothes and put them back in the wardrobe. They hugged their toys and said goodbye. They left their castle and went downstairs.

They hoped they could play again soon. They loved being kings and queens.

Lily and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They are very happy.

"Look, our snowman is so high!" Lily says. "He can see the whole park!"

"Yes, he is very high," Ben says. "But he is also very cold. He needs some powder to keep him warm."

"What is powder?" Lily asks.

"Powder is something you put on your face when you are sick," Ben says. "It makes you feel better. I have some in my pocket. I will show you."

Ben takes out a small bottle of powder from his pocket. He opens it and sprinkles some on the snowman's face.

"See, now he has powder on his face," Ben says. "He will feel better."

But the powder is not good for the snowman. It makes him sneeze. He sneezes so hard that his hat and scarf fly off. His carrot nose and rocks fall off too. He looks very sad.

"Oh no, what did you do?" Lily says. "You made our snowman sick!"

"I'm sorry, I didn't know," Ben says. "I thought it was good powder. Maybe we can fix him."

They try to put the hat and scarf back on the snowman. They try to find the carrot and the rocks. But the snow is too soft and the wind is too strong. The snowman falls apart.

They are very sad. They hug each other and cry.

"Maybe we can make another snowman tomorrow," Lily says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But we will not give him any powder. Powder is bad for snowmen."

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny thing in the grass. It was a gem that someone had lost. Sara wanted to keep it, but Tom said they should give it back.

"Whoever lost this gem must be very sad," Tom said. "We should find them and make them happy."

"But it is so pretty," Sara said. "I want to have it. It is mine now."

She put the gem in her pocket and ran away. Tom followed her, but he was angry.

Sara ran to her house and showed the gem to her mom. Her mom was surprised and asked her where she got it.

"I found it in the park," Sara said. "It is mine."

Her mom shook her head. "No, Sara, it is not yours. It belongs to someone else. You should not take things that are not yours. That is wrong. You should be sorry and return it."

Sara felt bad. She knew her mom was right. She had been foolish and greedy. She had hurt her friend and the owner of the gem. She regretted what she had done.

She took the gem and ran back to the park. She hoped Tom was still there. She wanted to say sorry and give the gem back.

"Tom, I am sorry," she said. "I was wrong. I should not have taken the gem. It is not mine. Can you forgive me?"

Tom looked at her and smiled. He took the gem and hugged her.

"Of course I forgive you, Sara," he said. "You are my friend. I am glad you came back. Let's go and find the owner of the gem. Maybe they are still looking for it."

They held hands and walked around the park. They saw a lady crying on a bench. She had a necklace with a hole where the gem used to be.

"Excuse me, lady," Tom said. "Is this your gem?"

He showed her the gem. The lady gasped and smiled. She took the gem and thanked them.

"You are very kind and honest, children," she said. "You have made me very happy. This gem was a gift from my husband. He is gone now, but this gem reminds me of him. I was so sad when I lost it. Thank you for bringing it back."

She gave them each a hug and a candy. Sara and Tom felt happy too. They had done the right thing. They had learned a lesson. They had been good friends.

"Let's stretch our arms," Tom said. "Maybe we can get it."

They stretched and stretched, but they still could not touch the sugar. They saw a chair near the table. They had an idea.

"Let's use the chair," Lila said. "We can climb on it and get the sugar."

They dragged the chair to the shelf. They took turns to climb on it. Tom went first. He grabbed the sugar and threw it to Lila. Lila caught it and put it on the table. Then she climbed on the chair and looked for more things to make the cake.

She saw a bottle of milk, a jar of honey, and a box of eggs. She threw them to Tom one by one. Tom caught them and put them on the table. They were happy. They had everything they needed to make the cake.

But they did not see their dad coming into the kitchen. He saw the mess they made. He saw the sugar, the milk, the honey, and the eggs on the table. He saw the chair near the shelf. He saw Lila and Tom smiling.

He was not happy. He was angry. He had a harsh voice.

"What are you doing?" he asked. "You are not supposed to play with the food. You are making a big mess. You are wasting the sugar. You are in trouble."

Lila and Tom were scared. They did not want to make their dad angry. They did not want to be in trouble. They did not want to make the cake anymore.

They said sorry to their dad. They said they wanted to make a cake for their mom. They said they did not know it was bad to play with the food.

Their dad sighed. He saw they were sorry. He saw they wanted to do something nice for their mom. He softened his voice.

"I know you wanted to make a cake for your mom," he said. "But you have to ask me or mom before you use the food. You have to be careful and clean. You have to follow the recipe. You can't just throw things around. Do you understand?"

Lila and Tom nodded. They understood. They said sorry again. They said they would help their dad clean the mess. They said they would learn how to make a cake the right way.

Their dad smiled. He hugged them. He said he loved them. He said he would help them make a cake for their mom. He said they would use less sugar. He said they would have fun. He said they would make their mom happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys of different colors and shapes. Sometimes they played in their room, sometimes in the living room, and sometimes in the bathroom.

One day, their mom told them to organize their toys and put them in the right boxes. She said she would be back soon and they should not make a mess. Tom and Lily nodded and said yes, mom.

Tom and Lily started to organize their toys. Tom took the red toys and put them in the red box. Lily took the blue toys and put them in the blue box. They were having fun and singing a song.

But then, Lily saw a red toy that she liked very much. It was a fire truck with a ladder and a siren. She wanted to play with it, but it was in Tom's box. She asked Tom if she could have it.

"No, Lily, this is my toy. It is red and it goes in the red box. You have your own toys in the blue box. Go away!" Tom said.

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like Tom's answer. She thought Tom was mean and selfish. She decided to take the toy anyway. She grabbed the fire truck and ran to the bathroom.

Tom saw what Lily did and he was very mad. He ran after her and shouted, "Give me back my toy, Lily! You are a bad sister! You are a thief!"

Lily locked the door of the bathroom and laughed. She said, "No, Tom, this is my toy now. It is red and I like it. You can't have it!"

Tom banged on the door and cried. He said, "Please, Lily, open the door. Give me back my toy. Mom will be angry if she sees this. Please, Lily, please!"

She only saw a bright flash and heard a loud boom. Then she saw nothing and heard nothing. She was gone.

Tom heard the boom and saw the smoke. He screamed and ran away. He was scared and alone.

Mom came back and saw the disaster. She saw the fire truck and the red box. She saw the bathroom and the smoke. She saw Lily and the fire. She saw Tom and the tears.

She was shocked and sad. She hugged Tom and cried. She said, "Oh, my babies, what have you done?"

"Wow, what a pretty stone!" Ben said. "Can I see it?"

Lily nodded and gave him the stone. Ben held it in his hand and admired it. He liked it very much. He wanted to keep it for himself.

"Can I have it?" he asked Lily. "Please?"

Lily shook her head. "No, Ben. It is mine. I found it. It is rare and I care for it."

Ben frowned. He did not like Lily's answer. He wanted the stone more than anything. He thought of a plan. He pretended to give the stone back to Lily, but he dropped it on the ground instead. Then he said, "Oops, I'm sorry. I dropped it. Let me help you find it."

Lily bent down and looked for the stone. She could not see it in the grass. She was worried. She loved her stone. She hoped it was not lost.

"Good night, Spot!" they both said.

They hugged mom and went inside. They were sleepy and happy. They dreamed of their wishes and the moon and the stars.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make muffins for their mom. They found a box of muffin mix and a big bowl. They poured the mix and some water in the bowl and stirred it with a spoon.

"Can I put the muffins in the oven?" Ben asked.

"No, I want to do it!" Lily said.

They both grabbed the bowl and pulled it. The bowl slipped and fell on the floor. The muffin mix splashed everywhere. Lily and Ben gasped.

"Oh no! We made a big mess!" Lily said.

"Mom will be mad!" Ben said.

They heard mom coming. They quickly grabbed some paper towels and tried to clean the mess. But it was too sticky and gooey. They could not repair it.

Mom walked in and saw the mess. She frowned.

"What happened here?" she asked.

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt bad.

"We wanted to make muffins for you, mom. But we dropped the bowl and made a mess. We are sorry, mom." Lily said.

Mom sighed. She looked at their faces. They looked sad.

"It's okay, sweeties. I know you wanted to do something nice for me. But next time, please ask me before you use the oven. It can be very hot and dangerous. And please be careful with the bowl. It can break and hurt you." she said.

She hugged them and kissed them.

"I love you, Lily and Ben. Thank you for trying to make muffins for me. How about we clean this mess together and then we can make some new muffins?" she said.

Lily and Ben smiled. They nodded.

"Okay, mom. We love you too. Thank you for helping us." they said.

They helped mom clean the mess. Then they helped her make some new muffins. They put them in the oven and waited. They smelled yummy.

When the muffins were done, they took them out and let them cool. They put some butter and jam on them. They gave one to mom and each took one for themselves. They ate them and enjoyed them.

They were proud of their muffins. They were proud of their mom. They were proud of themselves. They were happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they see a big bottle on the table. It is red and shiny. They want to know what it is.

"Look, Ben, what is that?" Anna asks, pointing at the bottle.

"I don't know, Anna. Maybe it is juice?" Ben says.

They climb on the chairs and reach for the bottle. They open it and smell it. It does not smell like juice. It smells funny.

"Yuck, this is not juice. This is wine," Anna says.

"Wine? What is wine?" Ben asks.

"Wine is a drink for grown-ups. Mommy and Daddy drink wine sometimes. They say it makes them happy. But we are not allowed to drink wine. It is bad for us," Anna says.

"Oh, I see. Then we should not drink wine. We should put it back," Ben says.

They try to put the bottle back on the table, but it is too heavy. They drop it on the floor. It breaks and spills everywhere. The wine makes a big mess.

"Oh no, we are in trouble!" Anna says.

"Quick, let's hide!" Ben says.

They run to their room and hide under the bed. They hear Mommy and Daddy come home. They hear them gasp and shout.

"Who did this? Who broke the wine bottle?" Mommy asks.

"Look, there are footprints on the carpet. They lead to the twins' room," Daddy says.

They follow the footprints and find Anna and Ben under the bed. They look scared and sorry.

"Anna, Ben, did you do this?" Mommy asks.

"Yes, Mommy, we did. We are sorry. We were curious. We thought it was juice. We did not drink it. We tried to put it back, but it fell," Anna says.

"We are very sorry, Mommy, Daddy. We did not mean to make a mess. We did not know it was wine," Ben says.

Mommy and Daddy sigh. They are angry, but they are also glad that the twins did not drink the wine. They hug them and tell them they love them.

"Anna, Ben, we are not happy with what you did. You should not touch things that are not yours. You should not climb on the chairs. You should not open bottles that are not for you. You could have hurt yourselves or made yourselves sick. Do you understand?" Mommy says.

"Yes, Mommy, we understand. We are sorry. We will not do it again," Anna and Ben say.

"Good. Now, let's go and clean up the mess. And then we will have some juice and cookies. You are lucky that we are not too mad at you. You are lucky that we have another bottle of wine for later," Daddy says.

Anna and Ben smile. They are happy that Mommy and Daddy are not too mad at them. They are happy that they have juice and cookies. They are happy that they have each other. They are lucky twins.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big tent with a sign that said "Spooky Show". They wanted to see what was inside.

They paid one coin each and entered the tent. It was dark and scary. They heard strange noises and saw shadows. They held hands and walked slowly.

"Look, there is a skeleton!" Mia said, pointing to a white thing that hung from the ceiling. "It has no skin or hair. It is just bones."

Tim felt afraid. He did not like the skeleton. He thought it was ugly and mean. He wanted to leave.

"I hate the skeleton!" he said. "It is scary and bad. Let's go, Mia!"

But Mia was curious. She wanted to see more. She liked the skeleton. She thought it was funny and cool. She wanted to touch it.

"I like the skeleton!" she said. "It is not scary or bad. It is just a toy. Come, Tim, let's touch it!"

She pulled Tim towards the skeleton. Tim tried to resist. He did not want to touch it. He screamed and cried.

"Help! Help! The skeleton will get me!"

The noise attracted the man who ran the show. He came out of a corner and saw the children. He was not happy. He had a frown and a loud voice.

"What are you doing here?" he said. "You are not supposed to touch anything. You are ruining my show. Go away, now!"

He grabbed the skeleton and shook it. It made a rattling sound. Tim and Mia were scared. They ran out of the tent. They did not want to see the spooky show anymore.

They hugged each other and said sorry. They learned their lesson. They decided to play something else. They looked for something fun and nice. They found a balloon seller. He had a smile and a soft voice.

"Hello, children," he said. "Do you want a balloon? They are colorful and happy. You can choose any one you like."

Tim and Mia liked the balloons. They each picked one. Tim chose a blue one and Mia chose a pink one. They thanked the balloon seller. He was patient and kind.

They played with their balloons. They felt happy and safe. They forgot about the skeleton. They did not hate anything. They liked each other. They were friends.

Anna and Ben were twins who lived in a big house with their mom and dad. They had many toys and clothes and books, but they were not happy. They always wanted more things, and they never shared with each other.

One day, their mom took them to the park to play with other kids. Anna saw a girl with a doll that had long hair and a pretty dress. She wanted the doll for herself, so she ran to the girl and tried to grab it.

"Hey, that's mine!" the girl said. "You can't take it!"

Anna frowned and pulled harder. The girl cried and held on to her doll. Ben saw what was happening and ran to help his sister.

"Give us the doll!" he said. "We are wealthy, we can have anything we want!"

The girl's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Anna and Ben fighting with her daughter over the doll.

"Stop that right now!" she said. "You are being very rude and selfish! How would you feel if someone tried to take your toys?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other and felt ashamed. They let go of the doll and said sorry to the girl and her mom.

The girl's mom smiled and said, "It's okay, we all make mistakes. Why don't you play together and share your toys? Maybe you can learn something from each other."

Anna and Ben nodded and followed the girl to a bench. She showed them her doll and let them touch its hair and dress.

"It has a nice texture," Anna said.

"Yes, it does," the girl said. "It's soft and smooth. Do you want to comb it?"

Anna smiled and said, "Yes, please."

The girl handed her a comb and they took turns brushing the doll's hair. Ben watched them and felt curious.

"Can I try too?" he asked.

The girl nodded and said, "Sure, why not?"

She gave him the comb and he gently ran it through the doll's hair. He liked how it felt.

"This is fun," he said.

The girl smiled and said, "Yes, it is. Do you have any toys you want to show me?"

Ben thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I have a car that makes noises and lights up. Do you want to see it?"

The girl nodded and said, "Yes, I do."

Ben ran to his mom and asked her for his car. She gave it to him and he brought it to the girl. He showed her how it worked and let her play with it.

They had a lot of fun together, and soon Anna and Ben forgot about wanting more things. They learned to share and be kind, and they made a new friend. They realized that being wealthy was not as important as being happy.

Once there was an otter who loved to use things. He was a proud otter and thought nothing was impossible. One day he was cleverly hopping around a pond, when a little bird flew down saying, "Hey! Can I use your things?" 

The proud otter stopped at once and answered, "Yes, you can use my things. But you must be careful with them."

Once upon a time there were two friends, a fox and a bear. The fox and the bear would often go to the beach to talk and play. But one day the tide came in very quickly and soon the beach was covered in water.

The fox and the bear began to talk and discuss. The bear said "The tide has come and we must leave!". The fox argued, "no, let's stay and have fun!".

The bear thought for a moment. "I have an idea. Let's leave now and come back tomorrow when the tide is lower. We can make sure the beach is tidy so when we come back we can still have fun."

The fox agreed and the two friends left. The next day the bear and fox returned. The beach was still and the sand was tidy. They had lots of fun that day.

The moral of the story is to always be thoughtful and to think before you act. Cleaning up after yourself and being tidy is important and helps the environment around you.

Tim and Lily are in the same class. They like to play with toys and draw pictures. But they do not like to share. They want to own all the toys and all the crayons.

One day, they have a big fight. Tim grabs Lily's doll and says, "This is mine now. You can't have it." Lily cries and tries to take it back. She says, "No, it is mine. You are bad. Give it back." They pull and tug and yell.

The teacher hears them and comes over. She is not happy. She says, "Stop it, both of you. You are being bad. You have to share. You can't own everything. You have to take turns and be nice." She takes the doll and puts it on the shelf. She says, "No one can play with this doll until you say sorry and make up."

Tim and Lily are sad and angry. They sit in the corner and pout. They do not want to say sorry. They do not want to make up. They do not want to share.

But then they see the other kids having fun. They see them playing with cars and blocks and puzzles. They see them drawing and coloring and smiling. They feel lonely and bored. They wish they had someone to play with.

They look at each other. They remember that they are friends. They remember that they like the same things. They remember that they have fun together. They feel sorry and ashamed. They say, "Sorry, Tim." "Sorry, Lily." They hug and make up.

They go to the teacher and say, "We are sorry, teacher. We were bad. We want to share. Can we play with the doll again?" The teacher smiles and says, "Yes, you can. But you have to take turns and be nice. And you have to play with the other kids, too. They are your friends, too." She gives them the doll and a car. She says, "Now go and have fun."

Tim and Lily are happy. They play with the doll and the car. They play with the other kids. They share and take turns and be nice. They have fun. They are good.

They started to get angry and frustrated. They blamed each other for taking the wrong pieces. They shouted and cried. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and the tears. She asked them a question.

"Why are you fighting over the puzzle? Don't you know that puzzles are more fun when you do them together? You need to unite and work as a team. Then you can see the whole picture and be proud of what you made."

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for being selfish. They decided to listen to their mom and unite. They said sorry and hugged. They put the pieces back in the box and started again. They helped each other find the right pieces and places. They talked and laughed. They enjoyed the puzzle.

Soon, they finished the puzzle. They saw the beautiful farm with the animals and the trees. They were happy and proud. They thanked their mom for the puzzle and for the lesson. They learned that being selfish is not good and that being united is better. They promised to share their toys and play nicely from then on.

They started to wrap their toys, their books, their pillows, and even their clothes with paper and tape. They made funny shapes and colors and laughed a lot. They were very playful and did not hear their mom calling them for lunch. They did not want to stop wrapping things.

Tommy liked to hop. He hopped in the morning, he hopped at noon, he hopped in the evening. He hopped with his friends, he hopped with his toys, he hopped with his dog. He hopped everywhere he could.

One day, he found a hat. It was a big hat, with a red feather. It was not an ordinary hat. It was a magic hat. Tommy put it on his head and hopped. He felt something strange. He looked around and saw that he was not in his yard anymore. He was in a forest, with tall trees and colorful birds.

"Wow!" he said. "This hat can take me to different places. I wonder where else I can go."

He hopped again and again, and each time he saw a new place. He saw a farm, with cows and pigs and chickens. He saw a beach, with sand and waves and shells. He saw a city, with cars and buses and buildings. He saw a lot of things he had never seen before.

He was having fun, but he also missed his home. He wanted to see his mom and dad and his dog. He wanted to play with his friends and his toys. He wanted to eat his favorite food and sleep in his own bed. He decided to hop one last time and go back to his yard.

He hopped and hopped, but nothing happened. He was still in the city, with the noise and the crowd. He tried to hop again, but the hat fell off his head. A man picked it up and ran away.

"Hey!" Tommy shouted. "That's my hat! Give it back!"

But the man did not hear him. He was gone. Tommy was sad and scared. He did not know how to get home without his hat. He did not know anyone in the city. He did not know what to do.

He sat on the sidewalk and cried. He wished he had never found the hat. He wished he had never hopped away from his home. He wished he had been happy with his ordinary life.

"Your boat is silly," Billy said to Tommy. "It is too small and slow and old. My boat is better than yours. I can sail faster and farther and louder. You are not a real pirate. You are a baby."

Tommy felt angry and sad. He did not like Billy. He wanted to show him that his boat was not silly. He said, "My boat is not silly. It is jolly. It is fun and brave and strong. I am a real pirate. I can sail anywhere I want. You are not a captain. You are a meanie."

They started to sail their boats in the pond. They tried to bump each other and splash each other and make each other stop. They shouted and argued and did not have fun. They did not notice that the wind was blowing harder and the water was getting rougher.

Suddenly, a big wave came and swept both boats away. Tommy and Billy watched in horror as their boats disappeared in the water. They ran to the edge of the pond and tried to find them, but they could not. They had lost their boats.

They started to cry. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had been nice to each other. They wished they had their boats back.

Then, they heard a voice. It was Tommy's mother. She had seen what had happened and came to help. She said, "What is wrong, boys? Why are you crying?"

Tommy and Billy told her what had happened. They said they were sorry. They said they were silly. They said they wanted their boats back.

Tommy's mother said, "I'm sorry you lost your boats. I know you loved them. But you know what? Boats are not the most important thing. Friends are. You should not fight over boats. You should share and play together. That is what pirates and captains do. That is what jolly people do."

Tommy and Billy looked at each other. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "You are right, mother. We were wrong. We should have been friends. We should have been jolly. Can we be friends now?"

Tommy's mother smiled and said, "Of course you can. Friends are easy to make and hard to lose. Boats are hard to make and easy to lose. Friends are more fun and more jolly than boats. Come on, let's go home and have some cookies. Maybe we can make some new boats later."

Tommy and Billy nodded and smiled. They hugged each other and said, "Thank you, mother. Thank you, friend. Let's go home and be jolly."

They walked away with Tommy's mother, holding hands and laughing. They had learned a lesson. They had learned to be jolly.

One day, her friend Ben came over to play. He saw the dragon and wanted to play with it too. He asked Lily, "Can I play with your dragon? It looks so fun!"

Lily said, "No, you can't! It is my dragon! Go away!"

Lily thought for a moment. She wanted to hear the lion roar, but she did not want to give up her dragon. She said, "How about we play with both? You can play with my dragon for a little bit, and I can play with your book for a little bit. Then we can switch."

Ben said, "That sounds good to me. I think that is a good idea. I recommend we do that."

Lily said, "OK, let's do that. But be careful with my dragon. He is very special to me."

Ben said, "Don't worry, I will be careful. And you be careful with my book. It is very special to me too."

They smiled at each other and started to play. They had fun with the dragon and the book. They learned new words and made new sounds. They shared their toys and became friends.

Tim and Mia like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads and bridges with their blocks and pretend to drive around.

One day, they find a box of matches in the kitchen. They do not know what matches are, but they think they look like little sticks. They take some matches and put them in their cars.

"Look, Mia, I have a brilliant red car with a stick on it!" Tim says.

"Me too, Tim, I have a brilliant yellow car with a stick on it!" Mia says.

They drive their cars to the living room, where there is a big rug. They see a candle on the table. They think the candle is pretty and smells good.

"Let's pull the sticks and see what happens!" Tim says.

"Okay, Tim, let's pull the sticks!" Mia says.

They pull the sticks on their cars. The sticks make a spark and catch fire. The fire scares them and they drop their cars on the rug. The rug starts to burn too.

"Help, help, fire, fire!" Tim and Mia scream.

Mom and Dad hear them and run to the living room. They see the fire and grab a blanket. They put out the fire with the blanket and take the matches away from Tim and Mia.

"Tim, Mia, what did you do?" Mom asks.

"We played with the sticks, Mom, we did not know they make fire!" Tim says.

"Those are not sticks, those are matches, and they are very dangerous!" Dad says. "You should never play with matches, they can hurt you and burn things!"

"We are sorry, Mom, we are sorry, Dad, we did not mean to make fire!" Mia says.

Mom and Dad hug Tim and Mia and tell them they are glad they are not hurt. They explain to them what matches are and how to be safe with fire. They also check the rug and the cars and see if they are damaged.

"From now on, only play with your toy cars, not with matches, okay?" Mom says.

"Okay, Mom, we promise, no more matches!" Tim and Mia say.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a playful dog named Spot. Spot loved to jump and play all day. He was always happy and full of energy.

One sunny day, Spot's owner, a little girl named Sue, had a task for him. She wanted Spot to help her find her lost ball. Sue said, "Spot, let's find my ball. Can you help me?" Spot wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, I can help!"

Sue and Spot started to look for the ball. They looked under the trees and behind the bushes. Spot jumped high and low to find the ball. Finally, Spot found the ball in a big pile of leaves. He jumped and grabbed the ball with his mouth.

Sue clapped her hands and said, "Good job, Spot! You found my ball!" Spot was so happy and proud. They both laughed and continued to play together in the park. And from that day on, Spot and Sue were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Clara. One day she went to the garden with her mom. She saw some small tomatoes. 

Clara asked her mom, "What are those?" 

Her mom replied, "They are tomatoes, sweetheart." 

Clara was so excited and asked, "Can I pick one?" 

Her mom said, "Of course, but be careful not to pick the small ones." 

So Clara carefully picked one small tomato and showed it to her mom. She was very proud of herself. 

Her mom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Clara!"

Lily and Ben were bored. It was a gloomy day and they could not go outside. They looked at their toys, but they did not want to play with them. They wanted to do something new and fun.

"Let's dress up!" Lily said. She ran to her room and came back with a big box. The box had many clothes and hats and shoes and bags. "We can pretend to be anyone we want!"

Ben smiled. He liked to dress up. He opened the box and took out a red cape and a mask. He put them on and said, "I am a superhero! I can fly and save the world!"

Lily giggled. She found a yellow dress and a crown. She put them on and said, "I am a princess! I live in a castle and have a pony!"

They played for a while, making up stories and adventures. They had fun and forgot about the gloomy day.

Then, Lily had an idea. She saw some paper and crayons on the table. She said, "Let's make our own costumes! We can draw and cut and glue!"

Ben liked the idea. He said, "Yes, let's do that! We can make anything we want!"

They took the paper and crayons and started to draw. They drew animals and monsters and aliens and robots. They cut out the shapes and glued them to their clothes. They made ears and tails and horns and wings.

They looked at each other and laughed. They looked very funny and silly. They said, "We are the best dress up friends ever!"

Once upon a time there was a fat bush in a meadow. Every day, a little girl named Mary went to the bush and sat down next to it. Mary spent hours playing with the bush, exploring the different ways she could value it. 

One day, Mary started to build a cozy home for herself and the bush. She found two sticks in the meadow and used them to create walls. The little girl also used some large leaves to make a roof. The bush watched happily as Mary added layers of soft grass to make the home comfortable.

At the end of the day, Mary lay down and hugged the fat bush. She felt a warm feeling inside her heart, realizing how much the bush meant to her. Mary had valued the bush's company in the meadow more than anything else. She smiled and fell asleep, knowing that she and the bush would always be friends.

The mouse offered the bear some tea in a special, unique cup. The cup was so colourful that the bear was filled with happiness. While they were chatting, the bear asked the mouse why he had such a special cup.

The mouse replied, "Every person is unique, like this cup! Always treat each person you meet with kindness, because everyone is special in their own way".

The bear was so glad to hear this message. He hugged the mouse again and thanked him for the cup of tea. From then on, the bear treated everyone he saw with respect and kindness, just like the mouse had said.
